Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy and his mom went to the grocery store. Timmy was very excited to buy some candy. When they got to the store, Timmy saw a sign that said "Free Candy!" He was so happy and he ran to get some.

But when he got there, he saw that the candy was fake. Timmy was very sad and he started to cry. His mom saw him and asked what was wrong. Timmy told her about the fake candy.

His mom hugged him and said, "Don't be sad, Timmy. Sometimes things are not what they seem. It's important to always check before you pack something in your bag. That way, you won't be disappointed." Timmy felt better and they went to buy some real candy. From that day on, Timmy always checked before he packed anything.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient woman living in a far away land.

One day, she was walking in the forest by herself when she came across a large popcorn tree. Amazed, she shook the tree and it began to rain popcorn.

"I'll pick some popcorn and take it home," the woman said.

But the moment the ancient woman reached out to grab some, it vanished right before her eyes.

"What happened?" the woman asked, puzzled.

Then, a magical voice spoke out from the tree, saying "Little children can see popcorn when you shake this tree. But if you pick it, it will vanish!"

The woman was so amazed. She thanked the magical voice and left the forest, happy that she had seen a popcorn tree.

Once upon a time, there lived a brave lion called Steve. He was determined to find victory and was always looking for an adventure. One day, Steve smelled the thick aroma coming from his neighbor's farm. It smelt like something delicious!

When Steve saw what was cooking, he knew he had to try it. His neighbor, a wise old goat, noticed him and said: "Do you want some of my stew, Steve? It's made from lots of different vegetables and it will make you bigger and stronger!"

Steve was thrilled and immediately gulped down the hot stew. But after finishing the meal, he realized something strange was happening. He felt like he was shrinking! Although he was scared, Steve managed to stay brave and faced his neighbor.

The boy turned around and said, "My name is David. I'm looking for the truth. Can you tell me where to find it?"

Ella said, "The truth can be found inside yourself. You'll know it when it feels right. It's not always fast, but it is never slow."

David smiled, thanked Ella and went off in search of the truth. Ella was so happy she could help David find the truth. She hoped that one day, she too could find the truth.

Then, Spot got a big shock. His friend, the cat named Whiskers, brought him a new bone. Spot was so happy to have a new bone to chew on. He even played with Whiskers for a little while. From that day on, Spot was not so lazy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she was playing with her friend Timmy when she saw a mosquito flying around them.

"Look Timmy, a mosquito!" Lily said.

"I don't like mosquitoes," Timmy said. "They always bite me and make me itchy."

Lily felt sorry for Timmy. "I believe we should go inside," she said. "So the poor mosquito won't bite us."

Later that night, Lily's mom came into her room to tuck her in. "Mommy, do mosquitoes bite poor people too?" Lily asked.

"Yes, sweetie," her mom said. "Mosquitoes don't care if you're rich or poor. They just want to suck your blood."

Lily thought about the poor mosquito and felt sad. She decided to always wear bug spray when she played outside so she wouldn't get bitten. From that day on, Lily and Timmy never got bitten by mosquitoes again.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a small house by the road. He liked to sit on his porch and watch cars drive by. One day, a little girl walked by and said, "Hello, old man. Do you like the road?"

The old man smiled and said, "Yes, I do. I've been on this road for a very long time."

The little girl asked, "Can you speak to the road?"

The old man chuckled and said, "No, I can't. But the road speaks to me. It tells me stories of all the people who have walked on it."

The little girl was amazed and said, "I want to hear the road speak too!"

The old man smiled and said, "You will, my dear. Just remember to listen closely and you will hear the road's stories."

The little girl walked away, happy and excited to listen to the road. And from that day on, she always stopped by the old man's house to hear the road's stories. The moral of the story is that if we listen closely, we can hear the stories of the world around us.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to pick berries. She would go to the garden every day and fill her basket with juicy red berries. One day, while picking berries, she heard a voice behind her.

"Hello, Lily!" said a little mole. "What are you doing?"

"I'm picking berries," said Lily. "Do you want to help me?"

"I can't," said the mole. "I'm too stubborn to leave my hole."

Lily giggled and continued picking berries. Suddenly, she saw a big bird flying towards her. The bird wanted to eat all the berries!

Lily quickly buried the berries in the ground to keep them safe. The bird searched everywhere but couldn't find the berries. When the bird flew away, Lily dug up the berries and shared them with the mole.

"Thank you, Lily," said the mole. "You're very clever!"

Lily smiled and continued picking berries, knowing that she had a clever plan to keep them safe from the stubborn mole and the hungry bird.

From that day on, the little birdie was famous among its bird friends for being so brave. It loved telling the story of how it dared to fly across the big bridge. And every time it saw the bridge, it felt a little bit braver.

So, they all ran to Bubba's home and settled inside. The hunter searched the forest but couldn't find them. Bubba and his friends were safe in their home. They were happy and grateful to have each other.

"Be careful, Tim!" Liz says. "The jar is heavy!"

"Uh-oh!" Tim says.

"Uh-oh!" Liz says.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the kitchen. She sees the mess and the children. She is not happy.

"What happened here?" Mom asks. "Who broke the jar?"

Tim and Liz look at each other. They are scared. They are pale.

"It was an accident, Mom!" Tim says.

"We are sorry, Mom!" Liz says.

Mom sighs and shakes her head. She picks up the children and hugs them.

"I'm glad you are not hurt, but you should not play with the cabinet things. They are not toys. They are dangerous. Do you understand?" Mom says.

"Yes, Mom. We understand." Tim and Liz say.

He grabbed his favorite car, a red one with a blue stripe, and ran to the door. He opened it and ran outside. He followed the truck down the street, making the same noise as the siren. Wee, wee, wee, wee! He repeated it over and over.

She finished making the sandwiches and went to get Tom and his sister. She went to Tom's room, but he was not there. She went to the living room, but he was not there. She went to the backyard, but he was not there. She started to worry. Where was Tom?

She looked out the window and saw the black truck coming back. It had helped someone and was going home. She also saw Tom, running behind the truck, still making the siren noise. He was very far from the house. He was in danger. There were many cars and people on the street. He could get lost or hurt.

She ran outside and called his name. "Tom, Tom, come back! It's an emergency! You have to come back!" She repeated it loud and clear.

Tom heard his mom's voice and stopped. He saw her waving and shouting. He realized he had done something bad. He had left the house without telling her. He had followed the truck too far. He had scared his mom. He felt sorry and scared.

He dropped his car and ran back to his mom. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry. I wanted to see the truck. I wanted to make the noise. I'm sorry."

His mom hugged him back and said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm glad you're safe. But you can't do that again. You can't leave the house without me. You can't follow the truck. It's dangerous. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded and said, "I understand, Mom. I won't do it again. I promise."

His mom smiled and said, "Good. Now let's go inside and have lunch. And then you can play with your cars. But only inside, okay?"

Tom smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. I love you."

They went inside and had lunch. Tom played with his cars. He still made the noises, but not too loud. He did not repeat the siren. He did not want to have another emergency. He wanted to be a good boy.

They ran to the park with their cardboard shoes. They saw Ben and the other kids waiting for the race to start. Ben saw them and laughed again. "Look at those silly shoes! They are not real shoes. They are trash. You will fall and hurt yourself. You will be embarrassed. You should not join the race."

Lily and Sam ignored Ben. They knew their shoes were not perfect, but they were proud of them. They had made them with their own hands. They had used their imagination and their creativity. They had not given up.

The race started. Lily and Sam ran as fast as they could. They passed some kids who had real shoes. They felt happy and strong. They reached the finish line. They did not win the race, but they did not lose either. They came in third and fourth place. They got medals and cheers.

Ben did not do well. He tripped on his shoes and fell. He scraped his knee and his shoes got dirty. He felt pain and shame. He did not get a medal or a cheer. He was embarrassed.

Lily and Sam went to Ben. They did not laugh at him. They felt sorry for him. They offered him their cardboard shoes. They said, "Here, Ben, you can have our shoes. We do not need them anymore. We hope you feel better."

Ben was surprised. He did not expect Lily and Sam to be kind to him. He had been mean and selfish to them. He felt sorry for himself. He said, "Thank you, Lily and Sam. You are good friends. I am sorry I was mean and selfish to you. I was wrong. Can you forgive me?"

Lily and Sam smiled. They said, "Yes, Ben, we forgive you. We can be friends. Maybe next time we can join the race together."

Ben smiled too. He said, "Yes, that would be nice. Maybe you can teach me how to make cardboard shoes. They are cool."

They all hugged and walked away. They learned a lesson. They learned that shoes are not important, but friendship is. They learned that being kind and generous is better than being mean and selfish. They learned that being creative and brave is better than being showy and proud. They learned that they can have fun and be happy with what they have.

Lily ran to the bathroom and opened the door. She saw Tommy sitting on the floor, playing with a toy car. She also saw the toilet, and she had a bad feeling.

She looked inside the toilet and saw Anna's pink dress and long hair. She was shocked and angry. She yelled at Tommy, "Tommy, what did you do? You threw Anna in the toilet! She is not a toy, she is my friend! You are a bad boy!"

Tommy looked up and saw Lily's face. He was scared and sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't know. I thought it was a game. Please don't be mad at me."

Lily was still mad, but she also felt sorry for Tommy. She knew he was only a baby, and he didn't understand. She said, "Tommy, you have to be careful with other people's things. You can't keep them or throw them away. You have to ask first, and be gentle. Do you understand?"

Tommy nodded and said, "I understand, Lily. I'm sorry. Can we be friends?"

Lily sighed and said, "Yes, we can be friends. But you have to help me get Anna out of the toilet. She is wet and dirty, and she needs a bath."

Tommy agreed and helped Lily get Anna out of the toilet. They took her to the sink and washed her with soap and water. They dried her with a towel and combed her hair. They gave her a hug and said, "We're sorry, Anna. We love you."

Anna smiled and said, "I love you too." She was happy to be with Lily and Tommy, who learned to share and care.

Ben and Lily are friends. They like to play games. Today they play a game with rice. They have two bowls of rice. They take turns to move some rice from one bowl to another. They count the rice in each bowl. The one who has more rice in their bowl wins.

"Your turn, Lily," Ben says. He moves three rice from his bowl to Lily's bowl. He counts the rice in his bowl. "One, two, three, four, five, six. I have six rice."

Lily smiles. She moves four rice from her bowl to Ben's bowl. She counts the rice in her bowl. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. I have seven rice. I win!"

Lily is curious. She likes to try new things. She says, "OK, what is the game?"

Ben says, "The game is called rice toss. We toss the rice in the air and catch it in our mouths. The one who catches more rice wins."

Lily thinks the game sounds fun. She says, "OK, let's play rice toss. You go first, Ben."

Ben nods. He takes a handful of rice and tosses it in the air. He opens his mouth and tries to catch the rice. But the rice is too small and too fast. He misses most of the rice. Only one rice lands in his mouth. The rest of the rice falls on the floor.

Lily laughs. She says, "That was funny, Ben. But not very good. You only caught one rice. My turn."

Lily takes a handful of rice and tosses it in the air. She opens her mouth and tries to catch the rice. But she is smarter than Ben. She does not toss the rice too high or too far. She tosses the rice just above her head. She catches most of the rice. Four rice land in her mouth. The rest of the rice falls on her hand.

Lily smiles. She says, "I caught four rice. I win again!"

Ben is sad. He does not like to lose. He says, "That is not fair, Lily. You cheated. You did not toss the rice high enough. That is not original. That is boring."

Lily is angry. She does not like to be called a cheater. She says, "I did not cheat, Ben. I played smart. You played silly. That is why you lost. And original does not mean hard. It means new and different. My way was new and different. Your way was old and same."

Sara liked to play with her shadow. She would run and jump and make funny shapes with her body. She would speak to her shadow and pretend it was her friend. She would say, "Hello, shadow. Do you want to play with me? You are very fast and big."

But sometimes her shadow was stubborn. It would not do what Sara wanted. It would hide behind a tree or a wall or a chair. It would change its shape and size. It would not speak back to Sara. It would only copy her. Sara would get angry and say, "Shadow, you are not nice. You are not my friend. You are mean and silly."

One day, Sara had a bright idea. She took a flashlight and went to her room. She turned off the light and closed the door. She shone the flashlight on the wall and made a shadow with her hand. She made a shadow of a rabbit, a bird, a dog and a cat. She spoke to the shadow and said, "Hello, shadow. Do you want to play with me? You are very cute and funny."

The shadow did what Sara wanted. It nodded and wagged and flapped and hopped. It spoke back to Sara and said, "Hello, Sara. I want to play with you. You are very smart and kind." Sara was happy and said, "Shadow, you are nice. You are my friend. You are fun and sweet."

Sara and the shadow played for a long time. They made more shadows and told stories and sang songs. They had a lot of fun. Sara forgot about her other shadow. She liked this shadow better. She said, "Shadow, you are the best. I love you." The shadow said, "Sara, you are the best. I love you too." They hugged and smiled. They were happy.

Lila was a horse who lived on a farm. She liked to run and play with her friends, but she was not happy. The farmer who owned her was very mean. He used a whip to make her work hard and did not give her enough food or water. He did not care if she was tired or hurt. He only wanted money.

One day, a man came to the farm. He had a big truck and a kind smile. He said he wanted to buy Lila and take her to a new home. The farmer agreed, because he wanted more money. He put Lila in the truck and said goodbye. Lila was scared, but she hoped the man was nice.

The man drove for a long time, until they reached a big city. Lila had never seen so many buildings and cars and people. She was amazed by all the modern things. The man took her to a stable, where there were many other horses. They were clean and healthy and happy. The man gave Lila a warm blanket, a soft bed, and a big bucket of water and hay. He stroked her mane and said, "Welcome, Lila. You are safe now. You will never suffer again. You will never see a whip again. You are free to run and play and enjoy life. You are my friend."

Lila felt a warm feeling in her heart. She nuzzled the man and said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. You are very nice. You are my friend too." She looked around and saw the other horses smiling at her. She felt like she had found a new family. She was happy.

Sara is a young girl who loves cheese. She likes to eat cheese with bread, cheese with fruit, cheese with crackers, and cheese by itself. She has a big cheese in the fridge that she wants to share with her friends.

One day, Sara invites her friends Lily and Ben to come over and play. They have fun with Sara's toys, books, and puzzles. Sara says, "Do you want some cheese? I have a big cheese in the fridge. We can eat it together." Lily and Ben say, "Yes, please! We love cheese too."

Sara goes to the kitchen and opens the fridge. She sees the big cheese, but she also sees something else. It is a small, furry, gray mouse. The mouse is nibbling on the cheese. Sara is scared and screams, "A mouse! A mouse! There is a mouse in the fridge!"

Lily and Ben hear Sara scream and run to the kitchen. They see the mouse too. The mouse is scared and runs away. Sara is sad and cries, "The mouse ate my cheese! My big cheese is gone!"

Lily and Ben feel sorry for Sara. They hug her and say, "Don't cry, Sara. We can get another cheese. We can go to the store with your mom and buy a new cheese. We are your friends and we love you."

Sara stops crying and smiles. She hugs Lily and Ben and says, "Thank you, friends. You are very kind and sweet. I love you too. Let's go to the store and get a new cheese. And maybe some cookies too." They all laugh and go to find Sara's mom. They are happy and hungry. They still love cheese.

Ben is a fat cat. He likes to rest on the sofa all day. He does not like to play or run or jump. He only likes to eat and sleep.

One day, Ben sees a shiny thing on the floor. It is a copper coin. Ben thinks it is a toy. He wants to play with it. He gets off the sofa and walks to the coin.

But the coin is not a toy. It is hard and cold and heavy. Ben tries to bite it, but it hurts his teeth. He tries to roll it, but it does not move. He tries to scratch it, but it makes a loud noise.

Ben does not like the coin. He is bored and tired. He wants to rest on the sofa again. He leaves the coin on the floor and goes back to the sofa. He curls up and closes his eyes. He is a fat cat. He likes to rest on the sofa all day.

Jenny and Ben were twins who liked to play in their room. They had a big mattress that they could jump on and pretend it was a boat or a castle. They also had a lot of toys and books that they could hang on the wall or on the shelf.

One day, Jenny had an idea. She said to Ben, "Let's make a tent with the mattress and the blanket. We can hang the blanket from the shelf and put the mattress under it. Then we can hide inside and read stories."

Ben thought it was a good idea. He helped Jenny hang the blanket from the shelf and put the mattress under it. They crawled inside the tent and picked a book. Jenny liked stories about princesses and Ben liked stories about pirates. They took turns reading to each other.

They were having so much fun that they did not hear their mom calling them for dinner. Mom came to their room and saw the tent. She smiled and said, "What are you doing in there, my little adventurers?"

Jenny and Ben peeked out from the tent and said, "We are reading stories, Mom. We made a tent with the mattress and the blanket."

Mom said, "That's very creative of you. But it's time for dinner now. You can play in your tent later. Come on, let's go."

Jenny and Ben put the book down and crawled out of the tent. They followed Mom to the kitchen. They were hungry and happy. They did not know that their tent was not very stable. The blanket was too heavy for the shelf and the mattress was too big for the space. As they left the room, the shelf broke and the blanket and the mattress fell down with a loud thud. The toys and books on the wall and the shelf also fell down and made a big mess.

When Jenny and Ben came back to their room after dinner, they saw the mess and gasped. They felt sad and sorry. They said to Mom, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not mean to break the shelf and make a mess. We just wanted to make a tent and read stories."

Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay, my loves. I know you did not mean to do it. But next time, be more careful with your things. And maybe use something lighter than a mattress and a blanket for your tent. How about a sheet and some pillows?"

Jenny and Ben nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. We will do that next time. Can we help you clean up the mess?"

Mom said, "Yes, you can. And then we can read some more stories together. You are very popular with me, you know."

Jenny and Ben smiled and said, "We love you, Mom."

They helped Mom clean up the mess and then cuddled with her on the couch. They read some more stories and felt happy again. They learned a lesson and had a good night.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a big book in their room. It had pictures of people doing exercise. They wanted to try some of the exercises too.

They opened the book and saw a man lay on his back and lift his legs up and down. "This looks easy," said Lily. "Let's do it." She lay on the floor and lifted her legs. Max lay next to her and did the same.

They saw a woman stand on one leg and touch her nose. "This looks fun," said Max. "Let's do it." He stood up and balanced on one leg. He touched his nose with his finger. Lily stood up and did the same.

They saw a boy sit on a chair and stretch his arms. "This looks good," said Lily. "Let's do it." She sat on a chair and reached her arms out. Max sat on another chair and did the same.

They were having a lot of fun doing exercise. But they did not notice that their dog, Spot, was watching them. Spot was confused. He did not understand what they were doing. He thought they were playing a game with him. He wanted to join them.

He ran to Lily and licked her face. She giggled and pushed him away. He ran to Max and jumped on his lap. He barked and wagged his tail. Max laughed and hugged him. He ran to the book and bit the corner. He tore the pages and shook his head.

Lily and Max saw what he did. They were angry. They shouted at him. "Spot, no! Bad dog! You ruined our book!" They chased him around the room. Spot ran away. He thought they were playing with him. He was happy.

The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to make things with leaves and flowers. They had a big box of scissors, glue and paper. They decided to make a surprise for their mom.

They cut some leaves and flowers with the scissors. They glued them on the paper. They made a beautiful picture. They were very happy.

But then they saw something mysterious. It was a big hole in the fence. They wondered what was behind it. They decided to peek.

They went to the hole and looked through. They saw a big dog. It was black and furry. It had a red collar. It looked at them and barked.

"Who are you?" Lily asked.

"Woof! Woof! I'm Rex. I live here. Who are you?" the dog answered.

"We're Lily and Ben. We live next door. We're making a surprise for our mom. Do you want to see?" Ben said.

"Sure. I like surprises. Can I come?" Rex said.

"OK. But be careful with the scissors. They are sharp. Come on, follow us." Lily said.

They went back to their garden. They showed Rex their picture. He liked it very much. He wagged his tail.

"That's very pretty. Your mom will love it. Can I help you?" Rex said.

"Sure. You can help us carry it to the house. But don't bite it. It's fragile." Ben said.

"OK. I won't bite it. I'll be gentle." Rex said.

They carried the picture to the house. They knocked on the door. Their mom opened it. She saw them and smiled.

"Hello, my darlings. What have you got there?" she said.

"A surprise for you, mom. We made it with leaves and flowers. And we have a new friend. His name is Rex. He lives behind the fence. He helped us too." Lily said.

"Oh, how lovely. Thank you so much. And hello, Rex. You're very welcome here. Come in, come in. Let me see your picture." she said.

They went inside. They showed her their picture. She hugged them and praised them. She gave them some cookies and milk. She gave Rex some water and a bone. They were all very happy. They decided to play some more. They had a lot of fun.

Lily and Ben were curious kids. They liked to explore the beach and look for shells and crabs. One day, they saw a big boat with a big anchor. The anchor was shiny and had a rope.

"Let's go see the anchor!" Lily said. "Maybe we can touch it and play with it."

Ben nodded. He followed Lily to the boat. They climbed on the boat and walked to the anchor. The anchor was heavy and cold. Lily tried to lift it, but it was too hard.

"Look, there is a button!" Ben said. He pointed to a red button near the rope. "Maybe it makes the anchor go up and down. Let's press it and see what happens."

Lily was not sure. She thought the button might be dangerous. But Ben was curious. He reached for the button and pressed it.

Suddenly, the rope started to move. The anchor lifted from the water and swung in the air. Lily and Ben were scared. They tried to run away, but it was too late. The anchor hit them and knocked them off the boat. They fell into the water and sank. They could not swim. They could not breathe. They were gone.

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They see a pigeon on the grass. The pigeon is gray and white. It has a red ring on its leg.

"Look, a pigeon!" Tom says. He runs to the pigeon. He wants to touch it.

"Wait, Tom!" Mia says. She follows him. She knows pigeons can fly away.

The pigeon sees Tom and Mia. It does not fly away. It does not move. It does not make a sound. It only blinks its eyes.

Tom and Mia reach the pigeon. They bend down. They are curious.

"Hello, pigeon," Tom says. He tries to pet it. The pigeon does not mind.

"Are you sick, pigeon?" Mia asks. She looks at its ring. She sees some letters and numbers. She does not know what they mean.

The pigeon blinks again. It does not answer. It is deaf. It cannot hear Tom and Mia. It only hears its own heartbeat.

Tom and Mia do not know that. They think the pigeon is friendly. They smile at it. They sit next to it. They share their bread with it. The pigeon eats some. It is hungry.

The pigeon likes Tom and Mia. It is not afraid of them. It is lonely. It lost its way. It does not know where its home is. It does not know where its friends are.

Tom and Mia do not know that. They think the pigeon is happy. They talk to it. They tell it their names. They tell it stories. They make it laugh.

The pigeon blinks again. It does not understand. It only feels their warmth. It feels safe. It feels loved.

"Wow, Tim, the hippo has big teeth!" Mia says.

They laugh and clap their hands. They want to get closer to the hippo. They see a fence around the water. The fence has a sign that says "Do not cross". But Tim and Mia do not read the sign. They think the fence is for fun. They climb over the fence and run to the water.

"Come on, Mia, let's touch the hippo!" Tim says.

"OK, Tim, let's go!" Mia says.

They run to the water and reach out their hands. The hippo sees them and gets angry. The hippo roars and splashes water at them. Tim and Mia get wet and scared. They scream and run back to the fence.

"Help, help, the hippo is mad!" Tim says.

"Help, help, the hippo is mean!" Mia says.

They climb over the fence and run to their parents. Their parents see them and get angry too. Their parents scold them and punish them. They make them sit on a bench and say sorry.

"Tim, Mia, you were very naughty!" Tim's mom says.

"Tim, Mia, you were very dangerous!" Mia's dad says.

"You did not listen to the sign. You did not respect the hippo. You could have been hurt. You have to say sorry and learn your lesson." They say.

Anna loved to play on the computer. She liked to watch funny videos of animals and draw pictures with colors. But her mom did not permit her to use the computer all the time. She said Anna had to do other things, like read books, play outside, and help with chores.

One day, Anna was very bored. She had read all her books, it was raining outside, and she had no chores to do. She asked her mom if she could use the computer for a little while. Her mom said no, she had to save the computer for later, when her dad came home from work. He had a big project to finish and he needed the computer.

Anna was miserable. She did not understand why her dad needed the computer so much. She thought he could finish his project on paper, like she did with her homework. She decided to sneak into the office and use the computer when her mom was not looking. She thought she could watch one video and then turn it off.

She tiptoed into the office and turned on the computer. She saw a lot of words and numbers on the screen. She did not know what they meant. She clicked on a button that said "delete". She thought it would make the words and numbers go away and let her watch a video.

But instead, the computer made a loud beep and the screen went black. Anna was scared. She had broken the computer. She heard her mom coming. She ran out of the office and hid under her bed.

Her mom saw the black screen and the delete button. She knew what had happened. She was very angry and sad. She called her dad and told him the bad news. He was very angry and sad too. He said he had to start his project all over again and he might lose his job.

Anna heard her mom and dad talking. She felt very sorry and guilty. She came out of her hiding place and said she was sorry. She said she did not mean to break the computer. She said she just wanted to watch a video.

Her mom and dad hugged her and said they loved her. They said they were sorry too. They said they should have explained to her why the computer was important and why she could not use it. They said they would try to fix the computer and finish the project. They said they would also try to spend more time with her and play with her.

Anna was happy. She said she loved them too. She said she would not touch the computer again without their permission. She said she would do other things, like read books, play outside, and help with chores. She said she would also make a picture for her dad to cheer him up.

The end.

Tom sees many animals, like chickens, ducks, horses and goats. He also sees some big bulls and cows in a field.

Lily wanted to show her friend, Tom. Tom came to see the flower and brought a fruit with him. He took a bite of the fruit and made a funny face. The fruit was sour! They laughed and played on the rug with the blooming flower. The rug with the flower was now their favorite place to be.

Once upon a time, a little boat was in the water. The boat liked to sail on the big sea. The boat saw many things when it sailed. It saw a big fish, a small fish, and even a very big whale.

One day, the boat saw a big statue in the water. The statue was very tall and had a harsh face. The boat was scared of the statue, but it wanted to be brave. So, the boat sailed closer to the statue.

As the boat got closer, it saw that the statue was not mean, but sad. The boat decided to be the statue's friend. They played together in the water, and the statue was not sad anymore. The boat and the statue became best friends and had many fun days sailing on the big sea.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big bookshelf in his room. He loved his bookshelf because it had many colorful books. The books had fun stories and pictures of animals, cars, and trees.

One day, Tim saw a small, fragile toy on top of his bookshelf. The toy was a cute little bird. He wanted to play with the bird, but it was too high for him to reach. So, Tim had an idea. He would rush and jump to get the bird.

Tim took a step back and ran as fast as he could. He jumped and reached for the bird. But, he did not catch it. Instead, the fragile bird fell and broke on the floor. Tim was sad, but he learned to be more careful with fragile things. He knew that next time, he should ask for help when trying to get something from the bookshelf.

Then, the dog found a gun. He did not know what it was. He thought it was a toy. The dog was being foolish. He wanted to play catch with the gun.

The cat saw the gun and knew it was not a toy. The cat wanted to keep the dog safe. So, the cat ran very fast and caught the gun before the dog could get it. The dog was sad, but the cat knew it was the right thing to do.

The cat and the dog went back to playing catch with a ball. They were happy and safe. The dog learned not to play with things he did not know.

Weeks later, Lily had saved enough money. She and her mom bought a bicycle for the little boy. They went to the park and saw the boy sitting on a bench. Tom agreed, and Mia went to hide the sharp toy knife. She hid it under a big pillow. Tom started to search for the toy, but Mia started to worry. She remembered that the sharp toy could hurt Tom. So, she quickly said, "Tom, stop! I will find it for you."

Mia found the sharp toy under the pillow and showed it to Tom. They both agreed that it was not a good idea to play with the sharp toy. Instead, they played with other toys and had a fun day. Mia learned that playing with sharp things was not safe, and she should always be careful.

Sue was worried about Max. She did not want him to get hurt. Sue had an idea. She said, "Max, let's play a game together. We can play hide and seek." Max liked this idea. He and Sue played together and had a lot of fun. Max did not jump over the rail again.

Anna said, "I'm sorry I scared you, kitten. You can play with my coins if you want. But please don't knock over the jar. And please don't hiss at me. Let's be friends."

He tiptoed closer to the dragon and reached out his hand. But the dragon opened one eye and saw Max. The dragon was not happy to see a stranger in his cave. He roared and breathed fire at Max.

"Who are you? What are you doing here?" the dragon said.

Max was scared and dropped his flashlight. He tried to run away, but the dragon blocked the exit.

"Please don't hurt me, Mr. Dragon. I'm sorry, I didn't know this was your home. I just wanted to see you. You are very beautiful and cool," Max said.

The dragon looked at Max and saw that he was just a little boy. He was not a thief or a hunter. He was just curious and adventurous. The dragon felt sorry for Max and calmed down.

"Thank you for your compliment, little boy. I'm sorry I scared you. I don't get many visitors here. Most people are afraid of me or want to take my treasure. What is your name?" the dragon said.

"My name is Max. What is your name?" Max said.

"My name is Blaze. I'm a fire dragon. Do you want to be my friend?" Blaze said.

"Yes, I want to be your friend. You are very nice and awesome," Max said.

Blaze smiled and moved aside. He let Max come closer and touch his scales and horns. He showed him his treasure and told him stories about his adventures. Max listened and asked questions. He learned a lot about dragons and had fun.

They became friends and talked for a long time. Then Max remembered his mom and looked at his watch. It was time to go back.

"Blaze, I have to go now. My mom is waiting for me. Can I come back and see you again?" Max said.

"Of course, Max. You are always welcome here. But don't tell anyone about me. I don't want to be in trouble. And be careful on your way out. The cave is dark and slippery," Blaze said.

"OK, Blaze. I won't tell anyone. And I'll be careful. Thank you for being my friend. Bye," Max said.

"Bye, Max. See you soon," Blaze said.

Max hugged Blaze and ran out of the cave. He found his flashlight and went back to the park. He saw his mom and waved at her.

"Hi, Mom. I had a great adventure. I met a new friend. He is very special," Max said.

"Really? Who is your friend?" his mom said.

Max smiled and said, "He is a dragon."

They waited until their mom went to her room and then they sneaked out of their bed. They took the drum and went to the backyard. They thought they could play there without anyone hearing them. They were wrong.

Their mom heard the drum from her window and came out to see what was going on. She was very angry and scolded them. She said they were naughty and disobedient. She took the drum away and sent them back to their bed. She said they would not play with the drum for a week.

Tim and Tom felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had made a mistake. They wished they had listened to their mom and been modest. They learned that playing with the drum was fun, but not when it was time to sleep. They learned that escaping from their bed was not a good idea. They learned that they had to respect their mom and follow her rules. They said sorry to their mom and hugged her. They promised to be good and never do it again.

Lily was sleeping in her bed. She had a dream about a pretty bracelet. It was pink and shiny and had many beads. She wanted to wear it and show it to her friends.

But then she heard a loud noise. It was her brother, Tom. He was playing with his cars in the living room. He made them go vroom vroom and crash. Lily woke up and felt angry. She did not like the noise. It made her head hurt.

She got out of her bed and went to the living room. She saw Tom on the floor with his cars. He was smiling and having fun. She did not smile. She said, "Tom, stop it! You are too loud! You woke me up!"

Tom looked at her and said, "Sorry, Lily. I did not know you were sleeping. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily shook her head. She said, "No, I don't. I want to sleep. And I want to dream about my bracelet. It is much nicer than your cars."

Tom felt sad. He said, "But I don't have a bracelet. I only have cars. And I like them. They are fun and fast. Can I see your bracelet?"

Lily said, "No, you can't. It is only in my dream. And you can't go in my dream. It is mine. Go away!"

She turned around and went back to her bed. She closed her eyes and tried to dream again. But she could not. She felt bitter. She did not have a real bracelet. And she did not have a friend. She wished she had both.

But Jill hated the night. She was afraid of the dark and the noises. She often had nightmares about scary things that chased her or hurt her. She would wake up crying and run to her mom's bed.

One night, Jill had a very bad nightmare. She dreamed that a big snake was wrapping around her and squeezing her. She could not breathe or move. She screamed for her mom.

"Mom! Mom! Help me!" she shouted.

Her mom heard her and quickly turned on the light. She ran to Jill's bed and hugged her.

"Shh, shh, it's okay, Jill. It was just a dream. You are safe with me. The snake is not real." she said.

Jill sobbed and clung to her mom. She felt her mom's warm and soft arms around her.

"Mom, I hate nightmares. They make me scared and sad. Can I sleep with you?" she asked.

"Of course, my sweet girl. You can sleep with me. I will protect you from the nightmares. You are brave and strong. And you are flexible. You can bend and twist your body in many ways. Maybe you can use that to escape from the snake next time." her mom said.

Jill smiled a little and nodded. She liked that idea. She followed her mom to her bed and snuggled with her. She felt safe and loved. She closed her eyes and hoped for a better dream.

He heard a giggle from the other side of the room. He walked over and saw a lump on the bed, covered by a blanket. He smiled and pulled the blanket away, hoping to reveal Lily. But instead, he saw their cat, Snowy, who was sleeping on the pillow.

"Meow!" Snowy said, annoyed by the disturbance. He stretched and yawned, then curled up again.

"Snowy, you are so lazy!" Ben said. "Where is Lily?"

"Here I am!" Lily said, popping out from behind the curtain. She had been hiding there the whole time, watching Ben and Snowy. She laughed and ran to hug Ben.

"You are so clever, Lily!" Ben said. "You tricked me!"

They both petted Snowy, who purred and closed his eyes. Then they decided to play another game, but this time, they let Snowy join them.

Mia and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They had a big pot, some spoons, and some salt and pepper.

"Let's make soup!" Mia said. "We need water and vegetables and spices."

"OK!" Ben said. He filled the pot with water from the tap and put it on the stove. He turned the knob to make the fire. "Be careful, Mia. The fire is hot."

Mia nodded. She opened the fridge and took out some carrots, potatoes, and celery. She washed them and cut them with a plastic knife. She put them in the pot. "Now we need some salt and pepper," she said.

She reached for the salt and pepper shakers on the counter. She shook some salt into the pot. Then she shook some pepper. But the pepper shaker was empty. "Oh no!" Mia said. "We have no more pepper. The soup will not be perfect."

Ben looked around. He saw a small jar on the shelf. It had a label that said "pepper". He took the jar and opened it. He smelled it. It was very strong and spicy. He smiled. "I found some pepper, Mia. Look!"

He showed Mia the jar. Mia looked at it. She saw that it was not the same as the pepper shaker. It was black and red and had seeds. She was curious. "What is that?" she asked.

"It's pepper," Ben said. "It says so on the label. It will make our soup perfect. Watch!"

He poured some of the pepper from the jar into the pot. He poured a lot. The pepper made a big cloud of dust. Mia and Ben coughed and sneezed. Their eyes watered. They could not see anything.

"Ah-choo!" Mia sneezed. "Ben, where are you?"

"Ah-choo!" Ben sneezed. "Mia, where are you?"

They could not find each other. They felt scared. They felt like they had disappeared. They wanted their mom.

"Mom!" Mia cried. "Mom!"

"Mom!" Ben cried. "Mom!"

Their mom heard them. She came into the kitchen. She saw the smoke and the mess. She saw Mia and Ben hiding under the table. She turned off the stove and opened the window. She went to Mia and Ben and hugged them.

"What happened here?" she asked.

"Mia and Ben tried to make soup," Mia said.

"But we had no pepper," Ben said.

"So we used this pepper," Mia said. She pointed to the jar.

Their mom looked at the jar. She saw that it was not pepper. It was chili powder. It was very hot and spicy. She understood why Mia and Ben had coughed and sneezed. She smiled.

"That's not pepper, my loves," she said. "That's chili powder. It's for making spicy food. It's too strong for soup. And for you."

Mia and Ben looked at the jar. They looked at their mom. They felt silly. They giggled.

"Oops!" Mia said.

"Sorry!" Ben said.

Their mom kissed them. "It's OK," she said. "You were trying to be creative. But next time, ask me before you use something new. OK?"

"OK!" Mia and Ben said.

Their mom took them to the bathroom. She washed their faces and hands. She gave them some water and milk. She made them feel better.

Then she made them some real soup. She used water and vegetables and salt and pepper. She did not use chili powder. She tasted the soup. It was perfect.

She gave Mia and Ben some soup. They tasted it. They liked it. They smiled.

"Thank you, mom," Mia said.

"Thank you, mom," Ben said.

Their mom smiled. "You're welcome, my loves," she said. "You're perfect."

Lila and Ben went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things in the water, like fish and shells and seaweed.

One day, they saw something new in the water. It was round and clear and had long strings. Lila wanted to touch it. She said, "Look, Ben, a balloon!"

Ben said, "No, Lila, that's not a balloon. That's a jellyfish. It can hurt you. Don't touch it."

Lila did not listen to Ben. She reached out her hand and touched the jellyfish. It stung her. She cried out loud. "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts!"

Mom and Dad heard Lila and ran to her. They saw the jellyfish and took Lila out of the water. They put some cream on her hand and gave her a hug. They said, "Lila, you should listen to Ben. Jellyfish are not balloons. They are animals that can sting you. You have to be careful."

Lila felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry, Mom and Dad. I won't touch jellyfish again."

Ben said, "It's okay, Lila. I'm glad you're not hurt too much. Do you want some ice cream?"

Lila nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, please. I like ice cream. It's tasty."

Mom and Dad bought them some ice cream. They ate it and felt better. They enjoyed the rest of the day at the beach. They did not complain anymore. They did not touch any more jellyfish. They had fun.

"Sure, but be careful. The barn is very old and some parts are broken. And mind the cat. He is very grumpy and does not like strangers," Mom said.

Tom and Lily ran to the barn and opened the door. They saw a lot of hay piled up in the corners. They also saw a black cat sitting on a beam. The cat had yellow eyes and a long tail. He looked at them and hissed.

"Hello, cat. We are Tom and Lily. We want to play with the hay. Can we be your friends?" Lily said.

The cat did not answer. He just hissed louder and showed his teeth. He did not want to share his barn with anyone.

"Go away, cat. This is our barn now. We will make a fort with the hay and have fun. You are mean and old," Tom said.

The cat was angry. He jumped from the beam and landed on Tom's head. He scratched Tom's face and hair. Tom screamed and ran out of the barn. Lily followed him.

"Ow, ow, ow! The cat hurt me! Mom, help!" Tom cried.

Mom heard Tom and came to the barn. She saw the cat and the hay. She saw Tom's scratches and blood. She was worried and angry.

"That cat is ancient and wild. He does not belong here. He is dangerous and rude. I will call the farmer and tell him to take him away," Mom said.

She hugged Tom and Lily and took them to the house. She cleaned Tom's wounds and gave him a band-aid and a cookie. She told them to stay away from the barn and the cat. She said they could play with the other animals instead.

Tom and Lily learned their lesson. They did not mind the cat anymore. They played with the dog and the horse and the cow. They had fun on the farm. They were happy and safe.

Once there was a fox who wanted to climb a tree. He studied the tree carefully and decided he wanted to climb the biggest branch. He took a deep breath and started running towards the branch. "Hey fox! What are you doing?" Asked the rabbit.

"You know, fox, sometimes things aren't meant to fit. Maybe you should try to learn something from this tree. Maybe you should visit it and look at it often, instead of just trying to climb it."

The moral of this story is that sometimes, instead of trying to "fit" something, it is important to just look and learn from it. By visiting something instead of trying to fit it you are now able to appreciate it more.

Moral value: The story teaches that talking is good, but being loud is not. It shows that being polite and respectful is important, but so is having fun. It suggests that finding a balance is the perfect way to be.

Mia liked to draw with pastels. She had many colors and made pretty pictures on paper. She liked to show her pictures to her mom and dad, who said she was very good.

One day, Mia found a new pastel in her box. It was black and shiny, and it felt cold in her hand. She wondered what it could do. She decided to try it on a blank paper.

She drew a big circle with the black pastel. Then she drew two small dots for eyes, a line for a mouth, and some spikes for hair. She looked at her drawing and felt scared. It was not a pretty picture. It was a mean face that looked angry and sad.

She wanted to erase it, but the black pastel did not come off. She tried to rub it with her hand, but it only made it worse. The black pastel smeared on the paper and on her hand. She started to cry.

She heard her mom coming to her room. She hoped her mom would help her. She hid the paper under her bed and wiped her hand on her dress.

"Mia, what are you doing?" her mom asked. She saw Mia's dress and hand covered in black. She looked angry and sad, too.

"Mia, did you use the black pastel?" she asked. She knew the black pastel was not for children. It was for grown-ups who made difficult art. It was not easy to erase. It could stain and hurt.

Mia nodded and sobbed. She was sorry. She did not know.

Her mom took her hand and led her to the bathroom. She tried to wash off the black pastel, but it did not come off. It burned Mia's skin and made it red and sore.

Mia screamed and cried. She wished she never used the black pastel. She wished she never drew the mean face. She wished she could make pretty pictures again. But it was too late. The black pastel had scared her and hurt her. And her mom was angry and sad, too.

One day, a little girl named Lily saw a black bird in the sky. She wondered what it was. She asked her mom, "Mom, what is that bird?"

Her mom looked up and said, "That is a crow, Lily. It is a kind of bird that has black feathers and makes a loud sound."

Lily said, "I like the crow. It is pretty and shiny. Can I be its friend?"

Her mom smiled and said, "You can try, but crows are not very friendly. They like to be alone or with other crows. They may not want to play with you."

Lily said, "But I want to play with the crow. Maybe it is lonely and needs a friend. Maybe it is an angel in disguise."

Her mom said, "Lily, angels are not black. They are white and bright and have wings and halos. They live in heaven and watch over us. They are very kind and good."

Lily said, "But maybe the crow is a different kind of angel. Maybe it is a black angel that helps the night and the stars and the moon. Maybe it is very brave and smart and strong."

Her mom said, "Lily, you have a big imagination. But you should not judge things by their color. Color does not make something good or bad. It is what is inside that matters. You should be nice to everyone, no matter what they look like."

Lily said, "You are right, mom. I should be nice to everyone. But I still like the crow. Can I give it some bread?"

Her mom said, "Sure, you can give it some bread. But be careful, it may not come close to you. It may be afraid of you."

Lily said, "Okay, I will be careful. I will not scare the crow. I will just say hello and offer it some bread. Maybe it will like me. Maybe it will be my friend."

Lily took some bread from her mom and went outside. She saw the crow sitting on a branch. She waved and said, "Hello, crow. You are very pretty and shiny. I have some bread for you. Do you want some?"

The crow looked at Lily and tilted its head. It made a loud sound and flew away.

Lily was sad. She said, "Bye, crow. I hope you have a good day. Maybe I will see you again."

She went back to her mom and hugged her. She said, "Mom, the crow did not want my bread. It did not want to be my friend."

Her mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily. But don't be sad. You did a nice thing. You tried to be kind to the crow. Maybe it was not ready to be your friend. Maybe it will come back another day. Maybe it will remember you and your bread."

Lily said, "Maybe, mom. Maybe. I still like the crow. I still wonder if it is an angel."

Her mom said, "Maybe, Lily. Maybe. You never know. There are many mysteries in the world. But you are my angel. You are my white and bright and beautiful angel. And I love you very much."

Finally, they saw an old man sitting on a bench with an open bag. The old man looked sad. Tom walked up to him and asked, "Is this your coin?" The old man's eyes lit up, and he said, "Yes, that's my coin! Thank you for finding it!" Tom gave the coin back to the old man, and he felt happy.

The moral of the story is to always be honest and help others when you can.

He reached out his hand to the snake, but the snake was not nice. It was envious of Tim's hand, because it had fingers and nails. The snake wanted to have them too, so it bit Tim hard.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tim cried. "It hurts! It burns!"

Sam ran to get their mom, who came quickly. She saw the snake and the bite, and she was angry.

"Bad snake! Go away!" she shouted, and threw a stick at it. The snake hissed and slithered away.

Mom took Tim inside and cleaned his wound. She put some medicine and a bandage on it. She hugged Tim and said, "I'm sorry, Tim. You were brave, but you were also foolish. You should not touch things you don't know. They can be dangerous and hurt you. Next time, listen to your brother. He was trying to help you."

Tim nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Sam. I learned my lesson. I will not touch snakes again. They are not nice. They are envious and mean."

Sam hugged Tim and said, "It's okay, Tim. I'm glad you are okay. I love you, brother. Let's play something else tomorrow."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you both, my boys. You are good brothers. Now, rest and get well."

"No, Anna, this is my car now!" Tom says. "It is more attractive than your car!"

Anna is angry. She grabs Tom's car.

"Fine, Tom, then this is my car now!" Anna says. "It is faster than your car!"

Tom is angry too. He tries to grab Anna's car back. Anna tries to grab Tom's car back. They pull and tug and yell.

"Stop, stop, stop!" a voice says. It is Mom. She comes into the room and sees Tom and Anna fighting over the cars.

"What is going on here?" Mom says. "Why are you fighting over the cars?"

Tom and Anna look at Mom. They feel ashamed. They know they are not being good friends.

"Sorry, Mom," Tom says.

"Sorry, Mom," Anna says.

Mom smiles. She takes the cars from Tom and Anna and gives them back to their owners.

"Tom, this is Anna's car. It is very attractive, but it belongs to her. You can ask her nicely if you can play with it, but you cannot grab it from her," Mom says.

"Anna, this is Tom's car. It is very fast, but it belongs to him. You can ask him nicely if you can play with it, but you cannot grab it from him," Mom says.

"Okay, Mom," Tom and Anna say.

They look at each other. They feel sorry for what they did.

"Tom, I am sorry I grabbed your car. It is a very fast car. Can I play with it, please?" Anna says.

"Anna, I am sorry I grabbed your car. It is a very attractive car. Can I play with it, please?" Tom says.

They smile at each other. They nod and swap their cars.

"Thank you, Tom," Anna says.

"Thank you, Anna," Tom says.

They hug and make up. They start playing with their cars again. They make them zoom and beep and crash. They laugh and shout.

Mom watches them. She is happy. She knows they are good friends.

Tim didn't believe Sue. He wanted to prove her wrong. So, he went to wash his hands with the fake soap. But no matter how hard he tried, the soap didn't make any bubbles. Tim was sad.

Sue saw that Tim was sad and said, "Don't worry, Tim. We can still play with the fake soap. Let's pretend it's real soap and play a game!" Tim smiled and agreed.

Together, Tim and Sue played with the fake soap, pretending to wash their hands and toys. They had a lot of fun, and Tim learned that even if something is fake, it can still be fun to play with.

Bella was a big dog who liked to run and play. She had a friend named Leo, who was a small cat who liked to nap and snuggle. One day, they saw a mysterious box in the yard. It was brown and had holes in it.

"What is that?" Bella asked.

"I don't know," Leo said. "Let's go see."

They ran to the box and sniffed it. It smelled like grass and dirt. They heard a tiny sound inside.

"Hello?" Bella barked.

"Help!" a voice squeaked.

They pushed the box open and saw a flea. He was very small and had a red hat.

"Who are you?" Leo asked.

"I'm Fred, the flea," he said. "I was in the grass, but a bird picked me up and put me in this box. Can you help me get out?"

"Sure," Bella said. "We can help you. Come on, hop on my back."

Fred jumped on Bella's back and held on to her fur. Bella and Leo ran to the grass and let Fred off.

"Thank you, thank you!" Fred said. "You are very kind and brave."

"You're welcome," Bella and Leo said.

"Do you want to play with us?" Bella asked.

"Okay," Fred said. "What do you like to play?"

"We like to race," Leo said.

"Race?" Fred asked. "What is that?"

"It's when you run fast and see who gets to the end first," Bella explained.

"That sounds fun," Fred said. "Can I join?"

"Sure," Bella and Leo said. "But you have to be careful. You are very small and we are very big."

"Don't worry," Fred said. "I am very fast and smart. I can race with you."

They lined up at the start and counted to three.

"Ready, set, go!" they shouted.

They raced across the yard, laughing and cheering. Fred was very fast and smart. He jumped from Bella's back to Leo's tail to a leaf to a flower. He reached the end first and waved his hat.

"I won, I won!" he cried.

Bella and Leo reached the end and smiled.

"You did, you did!" they said. "You are amazing!"

They hugged Fred and congratulated him. They played more games and had more fun. They became good friends and had many adventures. They were happy and free.

Tom said, "I will count to ten and you hide. Then I will find you."

Lily nodded and ran to find a good spot. She saw the bookshelf and thought it was a good place to hide. She climbed behind the books and waited for Tom.

Tom counted to ten and opened his eyes. He looked around the room and saw the toys, the bed, the closet, and the bookshelf. He wondered where Lily was. He walked to the bookshelf and saw some books sticking out. He pulled one of them and saw Lily's face.

Lily agreed and started to count. Tom looked for a new place to hide. He saw the rocking chair in the corner and thought it was a good place to hide. He climbed on the chair and covered himself with a blanket. He hoped Lily would not find him.

Lily counted to ten and opened her eyes. She looked around the room and saw the toys, the bed, the closet, and the bookshelf. She wondered where Tom was. She walked to the closet and opened it. "Found you!" she said.

Lily smiled and said, "You made a mistake. You rocked the chair and I heard it."

Tom said, "Oh, I did not know that. Next time I will be more quiet and still."

Lily said, "OK, let's play again. This time we both hide and Mom will find us."

But the chicken was too big and heavy. The crow dropped the chicken on the ground. The chicken made a loud noise. The dog heard the noise. He ran to the chicken. He saw the crow and the fox. He barked and chased them.

He looked down and saw that his ice cream was starting to melt. Timmy didn't want to waste any of his ice cream, so he quickly licked it off his finger.

When they finally got home, Timmy's ice cream was all melted. But that was okay, because he had already eaten it all anyway. Timmy was happy and his tummy was full. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Betsy. She loved to hop around in the garden and eat carrots. One day, while she was munching on a carrot, she felt the ground tremble. She got scared and her little heart started to beat fast.

She saw a big elephant walking towards her. The elephant looked very comfortable and happy. Betsy asked the elephant, "Why are you so happy?" The elephant replied, "I am happy because I am walking in motion. It makes me feel good."

Betsy was confused and asked, "What is motion?" The elephant explained, "Motion is when you move around and feel good. It can be walking, dancing, or even hopping like you do." Betsy understood and started to hop around with joy.

The moral of the story is that even when we are scared, we can find comfort in motion. It's important to keep moving forward and not let fear stop us from experiencing new things.

As he walked down the secret path, Max found a hidden pond with lots of fish swimming around. Max was so happy to have found this secret spot. He spent the rest of the day playing and swimming in the pond with his new furry friends. Max couldn't wait to travel back to the park and visit his secret spot again.

Lily was happy to hear that and she decided to try and draw more triangles. She asked her mom, "Mommy, can you teach me how to draw more triangles?"

Her mom said, "Sure, Lily. Let's try together. First, we draw a straight line. Then, we draw another straight line that connects to the first line. Finally, we draw another line that connects to the first two lines to make a triangle."

Lily tried her best to follow her mom's instructions and soon she was able to draw many triangles. She was so proud of herself and said, "Mommy, I did it! I drew many triangles. Thank you for being so kind and teaching me."

"I'm just munching on this leaf," replied the caterpillar.

Lily watched the caterpillar for a while, but then she got an idea. "I want to see what it's like to be a caterpillar!" she exclaimed. 

So, she picked up the caterpillar and put it in her pocket. She ran inside and found a big blanket to wrap around herself. "Now I'm a caterpillar!" she declared, wiggling around on the floor. 

But after a while, Lily started to feel uncomfortable. "Being a caterpillar is hard work," she said. "I want to reverse back to my normal life." 

She took off the blanket and let the caterpillar crawl back onto the leaf. "Thanks for letting me try out your life, little caterpillar," she said. "But I think I like being a girl better."

She chased the rabbit for a long time, until she spotted another hut in the distance. As she made her way across the fields, she spotted the same little rabbit hopping out of the hut. The little girl smiled, and followed it in.

Inside, she met an old man with a white beard who had been living alone in the hut. He welcomed her in, and they talked and laughed the whole afternoon. By the time the sun began to set, the little girl and the old man were best friends. The little girl sighed with joy.

The old man smiled and said: "Welcome to my home, little one. You can stay here forever."

And so, the little girl moved into the little hut and she was never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a pond. In the pond, there were two fish, one black and one white.

The white fish said to the black fish, "Let's swim and explore!"

But the black fish said, "No, we must remain in the pond."

The white fish was curious so it asked, "Why must we remain in the pond?"

The black fish replied, "Because the pond is filled with deep oil and it is dangerous for us to go outside the pond."

The white fish thought for a moment and then said, "I still want to explore. I will be careful and not get into any deep oil."

The black fish sighed and said, "All right, but you must remain close to the pond so you don't get lost."

The white fish agreed and off they went on their exploration. They looked around and enjoyed the sights and soon enough, they both returned safely to their pond and remained there forever, safe and sound.

The water was so deep that Tiny began to sink! He started to scream for help, "Help me! Help me!"

Just then, a wise old turtle emerged from the water. He calmly said, "Do not worry, Tiny. I will help you."

Tiny was relieved and said, "Thank you, Turtle."

The turtle nodded his head and then said, "All you need to do is soak yourself in the sun. The warm sunlight will crack open your shell and you will be free again."

Tiny followed the turtle's instructions and after a few minutes, he felt something crack open on his back and before he knew it, he was free again!

The turtle smiled at Tiny and said, "Now you can hop around as much as you like."

So from that day on, Tiny was always seen hopping around the pool, enjoying all the sunshine and water.

"Who will protect us?" asked one cub.

Momma Fox smiled. "We will protect each other. We'll look out for each other."

The three cubs smiled. They knew they could count on Momma Fox.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play on the beach with her friends. One day, Lily found a big, pretty shell that looked different from the others. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Tim.

"Look at my shell, Tim!" said Lily. "It's different! I want to keep it!"

Tim looked at the shell and smiled. "That's a nice shell, Lily. But I heard that if you whistle, something fun might happen!"

Lily was excited, so she put the shell to her lips and whistled. Suddenly, a little bird appeared from the sky. The bird danced around Lily and Tim, making them laugh.

Lily and Tim played with the bird all day long. When it was time to go home, Lily whistled again, and the bird flew away. Lily knew that her special shell was magical. From that day on, whenever Lily and Tim wanted to play with the bird, they would whistle with the shell, and their new friend would come to play.

"Wait, Sara!" Ben says. "Don't hurt the butterfly. It is small and pretty. Let it fly."

"I'm sorry, Sara," he says. "But you can't catch the butterfly. It is not a toy. It is a living thing. It likes to be free and happy. Maybe you can look at the butterfly and say hello. Maybe it will come to you and be your friend."

Sara wipes her tears and nods. She looks at the butterfly and smiles. She says, "Hello, butterfly. You are small and pretty. I like you. Can you be my friend?"

The butterfly hears Sara's voice and sees her smile. It feels curious and kind. It flies to Sara and lands on her nose. Sara giggles and Ben claps. They are both happy. They have a new friend. The butterfly.

"Come on, Tim, tell me," said Lily, moving closer. She saw a corner of the bag sticking out from under the desk. She reached for it and pulled it out. "Wow, Tim, you have so many cookies! Can I have one, please?"

"Sure, Lily, you can have one. And you can have one, too," he said, giving a cookie to Sam, who was sitting next to him. He saw that Sam's eyes lit up and he smiled. Sara peeked from under the blanket. She saw the medicine. She had an idea. She got out of bed and grabbed the medicine. She ran to the living room.

Lily was a curious girl who liked to explore new things. One day, she saw a big loop of rope hanging from a tree in the park. She wondered what it was for and how it felt to swing on it. She ran to the loop and grabbed it with both hands. She felt a rush of excitement as she lifted her feet off the ground and swung back and forth.

"Look at me, Mommy!" she shouted. "I'm flying!"

Mommy smiled and watched her daughter have fun. She was happy that Lily was brave and adventurous, but she also wanted her to be careful.

"Lily, be careful with the loop. Don't swing too high or too fast. You might fall and hurt yourself," she warned.

Lily nodded, but she did not listen. She wanted to swing higher and faster. She thought it was more fun that way. She pushed herself harder and harder, until she felt the loop slip from her hands. She screamed as she flew through the air and landed on the grass with a thud.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she cried. "Mommy, help me!"

Mommy ran to her and hugged her. She checked her for any injuries and kissed her boo-boos. She was glad that Lily was not badly hurt, but she was also sad that she did not listen.

"Lily, I'm sorry you got hurt. But you should have listened to me. I told you to be careful with the loop. You swung too high and too fast, and that's why you fell. Do you understand?" she asked.

Lily nodded, sobbing. She felt pain in her body and in her heart. She realized that she made a mistake and that she should have listened to Mommy. She regretted not being careful with the loop.

"I'm sorry, Mommy. I was curious about the loop, but I was also silly. I should have listened to you. You know what's best for me. I love you, Mommy," she said.

Mommy smiled and hugged her again. She forgave her and loved her too.

"I love you, Lily. I'm proud of you for being curious, but I also want you to be safe. Next time, listen to me when I tell you something. I only want to protect you and help you grow. OK?" she said.

Lily smiled and nodded. She learned her lesson and promised to listen to Mommy. She also learned to be more careful with loops and other things that might be dangerous. She still liked to explore new things, but she also liked to be safe and happy.

One day, a lizard was walking in the sun. He saw a big rock with a hole. He wanted to go inside and rest. But when he got closer, he heard a voice.

"Who are you? This is my home. Go away!" the voice said.

The lizard looked and saw another lizard in the hole. He was green and had a long tail.

"I am sorry. I did not know you live here. I am just looking for a place to rest. Can I share your home?" the lizard asked.

"No, you cannot. This is my home. You are too big and too red. You will take up all the space and make it hot. Go find another home!" the green lizard said.

The red lizard felt sad and angry. He wanted to fight the green lizard. He thought he was mean and rude. He opened his mouth and showed his teeth.

"Fine. If you do not want to share, I will make you share. I will split your home in two. Then I will have half and you will have half. How do you like that?" the red lizard said.

He moved closer to the rock and bit it hard. He tried to split it in two. But the rock was too hard and too strong. The red lizard hurt his teeth and his jaw. He cried out in pain.

"Ow! Ow! Ow! That hurts! Why did I do that?" the red lizard said.

He backed away from the rock and saw the green lizard laughing at him.

"Ha ha ha! You are so silly and foolish. You cannot split a rock in two. You only hurt yourself. You should have listened to me. I am wise and old. I know this rock well. It is my home and my friend. It protects me from the sun and the rain and the birds. It has a secret. Do you want to know the secret?" the green lizard said.

The red lizard felt curious and ashamed. He forgot his pain and his anger. He wanted to know the secret. He nodded his head.

"Yes, please. Tell me the secret. I am sorry I tried to split your home. I was wrong. You are wise and old. I am young and foolish. Can you teach me?" the red lizard said.

The green lizard smiled and nodded his head.

"Of course I can. Come closer and I will show you. The secret is this: the rock has two holes, not one. One is on this side and one is on the other side. They are connected by a tunnel. You can go in one hole and come out the other. You can rest in either hole. You can have one hole and I can have the other. We can share the home and the rock. We can be friends. What do you say?" the green lizard said.

The red lizard was amazed and happy. He did not know the rock had two holes. He thought it was a great secret and a great idea. He agreed to share the home and the rock. He thanked the green lizard for his kindness and his wisdom. He followed him to the other hole and went inside. He found a cozy and cool spot to rest. He felt peaceful and sleepy.

He closed his eyes and said, "You are a good lizard and a good friend. I am glad I met you. I learned a lot from you. I will not try to split things again. I will try to share and be nice. Thank you for teaching me."

The green lizard smiled and said, "You are welcome. You are a good lizard and a good friend too. I am glad you came. I learned a lot from you too. You are brave and strong. You have a big heart. Thank you for listening to me."

They both fell asleep and dreamed of the sun and the rock and each other. They were happy and content. They were friends.

"I'm not ignorant, Lily!" he said. "I'm smart. I found a good hiding spot. You're just mad because you lost."

Sam is sad. He does not like to be quiet and sit still and wait. He looks around the office. He sees a big chair, a big table, a big lamp, a big book. He thinks they are not useful. He thinks they are fun.

Sam has an idea. He jumps on the big chair. He jumps on the big table. He jumps on the big lamp. He jumps on the big book. He makes a lot of noise and mess. He thinks he is having fun.

Mom hears the noise and mess. She looks at Sam. She is angry.

"Sam, what are you doing? You are not supposed to jump here. You are making a lot of noise and mess. You are not being useful. You are being naughty. You have to stop jumping and say sorry," Mom says.

Sam stops jumping. He looks at Mom. He is scared. He does not want to be naughty. He wants to be useful.

"Sorry, Mom. I was bored. I wanted to jump. I thought it was fun. I did not mean to make noise and mess. I did not mean to be naughty. I want to be useful. How can I be useful?" Sam says.

Mom sighs. She hugs Sam. She is not angry anymore. She is tired.

"It's okay, Sam. I know you were bored. I know you wanted to jump. I know you thought it was fun. But jumping is not useful here. Jumping is useful outside, where you can play and have fun. Here, you can be useful by helping me. You can help me by sorting these papers, by drawing these pictures, by reading these stories. Do you want to help me?" Mom says.

Sam nods. He wants to help Mom. He wants to be useful. He does not want to jump anymore. He helps Mom by sorting, by drawing, by reading. He is quiet and still and useful. He is happy.

Mom is happy too. She finishes her work. She thanks Sam for helping her. She says he is a good boy. She says he can jump outside. She takes him outside. They jump together. They have fun. They are useful.

"Let's go and see the boats, Sam. Maybe we can find a nice boat to play with. A boat that won't pinch us," Lily said, wiping her tears.

Sam smiled and took Lily's hand. He agreed that boats were better than crabs. He hoped Lily would feel better soon.

"Okay, Lily. Let's go and see the boats. Maybe we can find a big boat that is ready to sail. A boat that will take us to a fun place. A boat that will make us happy," Sam said, leading Lily to the harbor. He wanted to make Lily smile again.

Ben listened to mom's story too. He wondered what would happen to the nosy cat.

Sara and Tom were friends who liked to play with boats. They made boats from paper and wood and put them in the pond. They pretended to sail to faraway lands and have adventures.

One day, Sara made a new boat that was very big and pretty. It had a red sail and a blue whip. She was very proud of her boat and wanted to show it to Tom. But Tom was jealous of Sara's boat. He thought his boat was too small and ugly. He wanted to have Sara's boat for himself.

"Wow, Sara, your boat is very nice," Tom said. "Can I play with it?"

"Sure, Tom, you can play with it for a little while," Sara said. "But be careful, it is very special to me."

Tom took Sara's boat and put it in the pond. He made it sail fast and far. He had fun with the whip and made it snap in the air. He forgot about Sara and her feelings.

Sara waited for Tom to give her boat back. She was sad and angry. She saw Tom having fun with her boat and not sharing. She wanted to get her boat back, but she did not know how.

Then, a big wind came and blew Tom's boat away. It sailed out of the pond and into the street. A car came and ran over it. It broke into pieces. Tom was shocked and scared. He ran to Sara and cried.

"Sara, Sara, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I broke your boat!" Tom said. "Please forgive me, I was very bad."

Sara felt sorry for Tom, but she was also hurt. She said, "Tom, you were not a good friend. You took my boat and did not give it back. You did not care about me or my boat. You only cared about yourself. You made me sad and you lost my boat."

Tom realized he was wrong. He said, "Sara, you are right. I was not a good friend. I was selfish and mean. I should have played with you and shared your boat. I should have been happy for you and your boat. I'm very sorry. Can we still be friends?"

Sara thought for a moment. She said, "Tom, I'm still sad and angry, but I also still like you. You are my friend. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me you will be nice and fair and kind from now on. You have to promise me you will not take things that are not yours. You have to promise me you will respect me and my things. Can you promise me that?"

Tom nodded and said, "I promise, Sara, I promise. I will be a better friend. I will be nice and fair and kind. I will not take things that are not yours. I will respect you and your things. I'm sorry, Sara, I'm sorry."

Sara smiled and said, "Okay, Tom, I forgive you. We are still friends. But you have to do something for me. You have to help me make a new boat. A boat for both of us. A boat that we can share and sail together. Can you do that?"

Tom smiled and said, "Yes, Sara, I can do that. I will help you make a new boat. A boat for both of us. A boat that we can share and sail together. That sounds like fun."

Sara and Tom hugged and went to find some paper and wood. They made a new boat that was bigger and prettier than the old one. It had a yellow sail and a green whip. They put it in the pond and sailed it together. They had fun with the whip and made it snap in the air. They were happy and they were friends.

The moral of the story is: Don't be jealous of what others have. Be happy for them and share with them. Don't take things that are not yours. Be nice and fair and kind. Respect others and their things. That's how you keep your friends and make new ones.
