She goes to her grandpa, who is sitting on a bench. He is old and wise and knows a lot about animals. He sees Lia's sad face and asks her what is wrong.

"Grandpa, I want to have a lizard as a pet, but it does not like me. It runs away from me every time I try to catch it. Why is that?" Lia says.

Grandpa smiles and hugs Lia. He says, "Lia, lizards are not like dogs or cats or birds. They are wild animals. They do not like to be caught or held or kept in a cage. They like to be free and live in their own home. They are happy in the garden, where they can find food and water and sun. If you want to have a lizard as a friend, you have to respect its nature and let it be."

Lia thinks about what grandpa says. She realizes that he is right. She does not want to make the lizard unhappy or scared. She wants to be kind and gentle to all animals. She says, "Thank you, grandpa. I understand now. I will not try to catch the lizard anymore. I will just watch it from a distance and admire its beauty. Maybe it will come closer to me if it trusts me."

Grandpa nods and says, "That is a good idea, Lia. You are a smart and caring girl. I am proud of you. Remember, the best way to have a friend is to be a friend."

Lia smiles and hugs grandpa. She feels happy and peaceful. She goes back to the garden and looks for the lizard. She sees it on a rock, basking in the sun. She does not run to it or shout at it. She just sits quietly and says, "Hello, lizard. You are very pretty. I hope you are having a good day. I am your friend. I will not hurt you or bother you. I just want to say hi."

The lizard looks at Lia with its bright eyes. It does not run away. It seems to understand Lia's words. It flicks its tongue and nods its head. It says, "Hi, Lia. You are very nice. I am your friend too. I will not bite you or scratch you. I just want to say hi."

"Sure, but be careful. It's not like your old train. It has a battery and a remote control. And it can make steam, like a real train," dad said.

He showed them how to turn on the switch, and how to use the remote control. He put some water in a small hole, and said it would make steam when the train was running. He put the train on the track, and pressed a button.

The train started to move, and made a loud "beep-beep". It went faster and faster, and soon it was zooming around the track. Sara and Ben clapped and cheered. They saw a puff of steam coming out of the train's chimney. It looked like a cloud.

"Can I try?" Ben asked.

One day, it was very hot. The sun was bright and warm. Lily wanted to play with her crayons. She took them out of the box. She put them on the table. She went to get some paper.

But when she came back, she saw something bad. Her crayons were not the same. They were soft and sticky. They were melting on the table. The sun was too hot for them. Lily was sad and angry. She cried and shouted.

"Why did you do this, sun? You ruined my crayons! You are mean and bad!"

The sun heard Lily. He felt sorry for her. He did not want to hurt her crayons. He wanted to make her happy. He had an idea.

He looked around and saw a bulb. It was on a lamp. It was not on. It was cold and dark. The sun shone on the bulb. He made it warm and bright. He made it glow like a star.

Lily saw the bulb. She stopped crying. She was curious and amazed. She went to the bulb. She touched it. It was not hot. It was nice and cozy. She smiled and laughed.

"Thank you, sun! You gave me a new toy! You are kind and good!"

The sun was happy too. He winked at Lily. He said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm sorry about your crayons. But you can still make lovely pictures. You can use the bulb. You can make shadows on the wall. You can have fun with light and dark."

Lily liked the sun's idea. She took the bulb. She turned off the lamp. She made shadows on the wall. She made shapes and animals. She had fun with light and dark. She forgot about her crayons. She was happy again.

Then I could hear everything better." Benny thought about it and realized that his big ears were not just for show, but they were also very useful.

From that day on, Benny was even more proud of his big ears. He realized that everyone has something special about them that they should be proud of. And he also learned that it's important to use what you have to make things better, like adding blocks to make a tower taller.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very shy and always stood behind her mommy's legs when she met someone new. One day, Lily and her mommy went for a walk in the park. They saw a lot of waste on the ground, which made Lily sad.

"Mommy, why is there so much waste on the ground?" asked Lily.

"I don't know, sweetie. People should throw their waste in the trash can," replied her mommy.

Suddenly, Lily saw a little bird standing on a tree branch. She said, "Look, mommy! The bird is standing on the branch. It's so cute!"

Lily's mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it is cute. Let's go say hi to the bird."

Lily felt a little shy, but she followed her mommy to the tree. When they got closer, the bird flew away. Lily was sad, but her mommy said, "It's okay, sweetie. We'll see more birds another day."

Lily smiled and felt happy again. She learned that even though she was shy, she could still have fun and enjoy the world around her.

Hoppy was curious, so he hopped over to the rock to take a closer look. He noticed that there was a little bird sitting on top of the rock. The bird was tired and couldn't fly anymore. Hoppy felt sad for the little bird, so he decided to help.

Lily put on the dress and the crown. "Now I'm a princess!" she said. Max smiled and they played all day in the warm sun by the castle. They had so much fun and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big tree, there lived a bird named Bob. Bob wanted to create a beautiful nest. He looked for sticks, leaves, and grass to make his nest attractive.

One day, Bob met another bird named Sally. Sally said, "Bob, I like your nest! It is so pretty!" Bob felt happy and said, "Thank you, Sally! I worked hard to make it nice."

Bob and Sally became good friends. They played and shared food together. Bob learned that being kind and sharing made his nest even more attractive. And all the birds in the tree became friends too.

The moral of the story is that being kind and sharing with others makes your home a happy and beautiful place.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a gloomy day. The sky was full of dark clouds. A little girl named Amy was sad. She wanted to play outside with her friends. But the rain made it hard to play.

Amy had an idea. She called her friends on the phone. "Let's make a club!" she said. "We can play inside and have fun even on gloomy days." Her friends liked the idea. They all came to Amy's house to start the club.

At first, the club was fun. They played games and laughed. But soon, Amy and her friends began to argue. They could not agree on what games to play. The club was not fun anymore.

Amy's mom saw the problem. She called the kids together. "Why don't you take turns picking games?" she suggested. The kids thought it was a good idea.

From that day on, the club was fun again. Amy and her friends took turns picking games. They learned to play together even on gloomy days. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very impatient. He did not like to wait for anything. One day, Tim wanted to wear his new red shoes. He put them on and went outside to play.

Tim saw a big sink in the park. He wanted to see what was in it. He ran to the sink and looked inside. He saw a little frog. The frog said, "Hi, Tim! I like your red shoes!" Tim was happy that the frog liked his shoes.

Tim played with the frog all day. They had so much fun. The sun started to go down, and it was time for Tim to go home. He said goodbye to the frog and went back to his house. Tim was not impatient anymore, because he learned that good things come to those who wait.

One day, a lovely little girl named Mia went to the garden. She saw a big radish in the ground. Mia wanted to pull it out, but it was stuck. She tried and tried, but she could not solve the problem.

Then, Mia asked her friend Tim for help. Tim came to the garden and saw the big radish. He said, "Let's try together, Mia!" They both pulled and pulled, but the radish was still stuck.

Finally, Mia and Tim asked their dog, Spot, to help. Spot grabbed the radish with his teeth. All three of them pulled together. "One, two, three, pull!" they said. And out came the big radish! Mia, Tim, and Spot were very happy that they solved the problem. They shared the big radish and had a lovely day in the garden.

One day, a fast car named Zoom loved to race around the town. Zoom was very proud of how fast he could go. He had a friend named Spear, who was a mild and kind bird. Spear was not as fast as Zoom, but they liked to play together.

One day, Zoom and Spear decided to have a race to see who was the fastest. Zoom was sure he would win. They started the race, and Zoom went very fast, leaving Spear behind. Zoom was so sure he would win that he stopped to rest under a tree.

While Zoom was resting, Spear kept flying, slow and steady. He did not stop to rest, even though he was tired. Zoom saw Spear flying and thought he still had time to win the race. So, he stayed under the tree a little longer.

When Zoom finally decided to finish the race, he was shocked to see that Spear had already crossed the finish line. Zoom learned that being slow and steady can sometimes be better than being fast. He also learned to be humble and not to underestimate his friends.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim was a very curious boy, but sometimes he was a little ignorant. He loved to watch the sunrise every morning.

One day, Tim saw an ice cream truck. He asked the ice cream man, "What happens to ice cream in the sun?" The ice cream man smiled and said, "It will melt, Tim. The sun is very hot and makes the ice cream soft and drippy."

The next morning, Tim woke up early to watch the sunrise. He remembered what the ice cream man had said about the sun melting the ice cream. So, he decided to try it himself. He took a scoop of ice cream and put it on a plate.

As the sun came up, the ice cream began to melt. Tim watched in amazement as the ice cream turned into a puddle. He learned something new that day and was no longer ignorant about what happens to ice cream in the sun.

From then on, every time Tim saw a sunrise, he remembered the day he learned about melting ice cream. And he always made sure to eat his ice cream quickly, so it wouldn't melt in the sun.

One day, a little boy named Tim came to the man. He said, "I want to buy some steam, please." The man smiled and said, "Okay, Tim. Here is some steam for you." Tim was very happy and played with the steam. But, the steam tasted bitter. Tim did not like the bitter taste.

Tim went back to the man and said, "I don't like the bitter steam. Can I have sweet steam, please?" The man thought for a moment and then said, "I will try to make sweet steam for you, Tim." He worked hard to make sweet steam and soon, the steam was sweet. Tim and the other kids were very happy to play with the sweet steam. They all had fun and the man felt very good to see them happy.

"I didn't mean to hurt you," Tim said. "I just wanted to show you to my mom." The beetle told Tim that it was okay, but to be more gentle next time. Tim and the beetle became friends and played in the garden all day.

Lily was happy and they both hung on the swing together. Max was not grumpy anymore. He learned that playing with friends is more fun than being alone.

Tom is a bird who likes to fly high in the sky. He has blue feathers and a long tail. He has a friend named Sue, who is also a bird. Sue has red feathers and a short tail. They like to play together and sing songs.

One day, Tom and Sue see a big cloud. It is dark and scary. It makes a loud noise like thunder. Tom and Sue are afraid. They want to go back to their nest.

"Tom, let's go home!" Sue says. "The cloud is bad. It can hurt us."

But Tom is curious. He wants to see what is in the cloud. He thinks it might be fun.

"No, Sue, let's go to the cloud!" Tom says. "Maybe we can find something new. Maybe we can make friends with the cloud."

Tom flies towards the cloud. Sue follows him. She does not want to leave him alone.

They get closer and closer to the cloud. The wind is strong and rough. It pushes them and pulls them. The cloud is wet and cold. It covers them and makes them wet.

"Tom, I don't like this!" Sue says. "The cloud is not nice. It is mean. It makes us wet and cold. It hurts our wings. Let's go back!"

But Tom does not listen. He wants to see more. He flies deeper into the cloud. He thinks he sees something shiny.

"Look, Sue, look!" Tom says. "I see something shiny. Maybe it is a treasure. Maybe it is a friend. Let's go and see!"

Tom flies towards the shiny thing. Sue follows him. She is scared and sad.

They get to the shiny thing. It is not a treasure. It is not a friend. It is a big metal bird. It has no feathers. It has no tail. It has a big mouth that makes fire and smoke. It is loud and angry. It sees Tom and Sue.

"Go away, little birds!" the metal bird says. "This is my cloud. You are not welcome here. You are too small and weak. I will eat you!"

The metal bird opens its mouth. It shoots fire and smoke at Tom and Sue. They are very afraid. They try to fly away. But the fire and smoke are fast and hot. They burn their wings. They make them fall.

"Tom, Sue, help!" they call. "We are in trouble. We need help. We want to go home."

But no one hears them. No one helps them. They fall and fall. They hit the ground. They are hurt and sad. They cry and cry.

They wish they had listened to Sue. They wish they had not gone to the cloud. They wish they had stayed home. They wish they had been happy.

"Oh, no, Sara, I'm so sorry. That fly is very naughty. It should not go in your jelly. Here, let me give you a new slice of bread with jelly. And I will throw away this one with the fly."

One day, they hear a loud noise outside. They look out the window and see a big truck. The truck is carrying many boxes. The boxes have words on them, but Sara and Ben cannot read them. They are curious about what is inside the boxes.

"Let's go see the truck!" Sara says to Ben.

"OK, but we have to be careful," Ben says.

They rush to the door and put on their shoes. They hold hands and run to the street. They see the truck driver get out of the truck. He is tall and strong. He opens the back of the truck and starts to take out the boxes.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Do you want to see what I have?"

"Yes, please!" Sara and Ben say.

The truck driver smiles and picks up a small box. He opens it and shows them what is inside. It is a pastel. But not a normal pastel. It is a very big pastel. It is bigger than Sara and Ben's heads. It is bright red.

"Wow!" Sara and Ben say.

"This is a special pastel," the truck driver says. "It is for making giant drawings on walls and buildings. Do you want to try it?"

"Yes, please!" Sara and Ben say again.

The truck driver gives them the pastel and shows them a blank wall nearby. He tells them to be creative and have fun. He says he will be back soon.

Sara and Ben are very excited. They take the pastel and go to the wall. They try to lift the pastel, but it is very heavy. They use both hands and struggle to move it. They feel weak.

"This pastel is too big for us," Sara says.

"Yes, it is," Ben says.

They look at the wall and see a small mark. It is the only mark they can make with the pastel. It is not a flower, or an animal, or a rainbow. It is just a red dot.

They look at each other and feel sad. They want to make a beautiful picture, but they cannot.

"Is that your masterpiece?" he asks.

Sara and Ben nod. They feel shy.

They feel strong. They feel proud. They feel happy.

Tom was surprised and happy. He said, "Hi, I'm Tom. Thank you for liking my whistling. I can teach you how to whistle. It's easy and fun. You just have to make a small hole with your lips and blow air through it. Like this." He showed her how to whistle and she tried to copy him.

"Can you find another match?" Ben asks, looking at his other cards.

Sara looks at her cards too. She sees a card with a big B on it. She looks for another card with a B.

"I have a B card, do you have one?" Sara asks.

Ben looks at his cards. He does not have a B card. He has a C card, a D card, and an E card.

"No, I don't have a B card," Ben says, shaking his head.

"That's okay, we can look for another match," Sara says, being kind. She does not want Ben to feel sad.

She puts her B card aside and picks another card. She has an E card.

"I have an E card, do you have one?" Sara asks.

Ben looks at his cards. He has an E card too.

"Yes, I have an E card," Ben says, happy. He shows his card with a small e on it.

"They match, they are both E," Sara says, clapping. She puts her card next to Ben's card.

Bunny was a little rabbit who loved to hop. He hopped all day long, from his home in the woods to the town where he had many friends. He hopped to the bakery, where he got a carrot cake from Mrs. Mouse. He hopped to the park, where he played with Mr. Dog and Miss. Cat. He hopped to the library, where he borrowed a book from Mr. Owl.

One day, Bunny hopped too much. He hopped all over the town, but he forgot to rest. He felt very tired, but he wanted to hop more. He hopped to the pond, where he saw Mr. Frog.

"Hello, Bunny," said Mr. Frog. "Do you want to hop with me?"

Bunny nodded. He liked Mr. Frog, who was a good hopper. They hopped together, from one lily pad to another. But Bunny was so tired, he could not hop well. He slipped and fell into the water.

"Splash!" Bunny was wet and cold. He cried out loud.

"Help, help!" he shouted. "I can't swim!"

Mr. Frog heard him and quickly hopped to him. He grabbed Bunny by the ears and pulled him out of the water.

"Are you okay, Bunny?" asked Mr. Frog.

Bunny coughed and shivered. He was scared and sad.

"Thank you, Mr. Frog," he said. "You saved me. I'm sorry, I hopped too much. I'm very tired."

Mr. Frog smiled. He wrapped Bunny in a warm towel and gave him a hug.

"Don't worry, Bunny," he said. "Everyone makes mistakes. You just need to rest and be careful. Next time, hop less and enjoy more."

Bunny nodded. He learned his lesson. He thanked Mr. Frog again and hopped back to his home. He ate some carrot cake, read his book and fell asleep. He dreamed of hopping, but not too much. He was happy.

"Yes, Ben, let's do it!" Mia says.

They take the file and go to a table. They start to draw with their colors. Ben draws a car, Mia draws a flower. They are happy and have fun.

But then, Sam comes to the table. Sam is a big boy who likes to take things from others. He sees the file and wants it.

"Hey, what are you doing with my file?" Sam says.

"Your file? This is not your file, Sam. We found it in the classroom. It is for everyone to use," Ben says.

"No, it is mine. I saw it first. Give it to me now!" Sam says.

He tries to grab the file from Ben and Mia. But they hold it tight. They do not want to give it to Sam. They are scared and angry.

"Stop, Sam, you are not nice. You cannot take our file. We are drawing with it. We want to finish our pictures," Mia says.

"I don't care. I want the file. It is big and has many papers. I can use it for anything I want. Your pictures are silly and boring. Mine are better and unique," Sam says.

He pulls harder on the file. Ben and Mia pull back. The file is torn in half. The papers fall on the floor. Some of them are ripped and dirty. Ben and Mia's pictures are ruined. They are sad and cry.

Sam looks at the file and the papers. He is not happy either. He sees that his pictures are not unique. They are the same as the ones he always draws. He feels sorry for what he did.

"Sorry, Ben, sorry, Mia. I was wrong. I should not have taken your file. I should have asked you nicely. I should have shared with you. Your pictures are not silly and boring. They are different and beautiful. Can we be friends?" Sam says.

Ben and Mia look at Sam. They see that he is sorry. They forgive him. They hug him.

"Yes, Sam, we can be friends. But next time, please be nice and share. Then we can all have fun and make more pictures," Ben says.

"OK, Ben, OK, Mia. I will be nice and share. And I will try to make different and beautiful pictures too. Maybe we can finish them together," Sam says.

They smile and pick up the papers. They find a new file and put them inside. They go to another table and start to draw again. They are happy and have fun.

The moral value of the story is: Sharing is caring. Do not take things from others without asking. Respect their work and feelings. Be creative and appreciate diversity.

One day, Lily saw a big carrot on the ground. She was hungry and wanted to eat it. She did not know that it was a trap. A mean farmer had put it there to catch bunnies.

"Look, a carrot!" Lily said to her friends. "I want to eat it!"

"Wait, Lily!" Max said. "It could be a trap. It is not safe to go alone. Let me go with you and check."

"No, I can do it by myself!" Lily said. She did not listen to Max. She ran to the carrot and bit it.

Snap! The trap closed around Lily. She was stuck and scared. She cried for help.

"Lily!" Max and Daisy heard her cry. They ran to the trap and saw Lily inside. They felt sorry for her.

"Don't worry, Lily!" Daisy said. "We will help you. We are your friends."

Max and Daisy worked together to open the trap. They used their teeth and claws and pushed and pulled. After a while, they freed Lily. Lily was happy and grateful.

"Thank you, Max and Daisy!" Lily said. "You are the best friends ever. I am sorry I did not listen to you. You were right. It was a trap. I was silly and greedy."

"It's okay, Lily." Max said. "We all make mistakes. The important thing is to learn from them. And to listen to your friends. They care about you and want to protect you."

"Yes, you are right." Lily said. "I learned my lesson. I will never go to a trap again. And I will always listen to my friends. They are smarter and kinder than a carrot."

The end.

Moral value: Listen to your friends. They know what is best for you. Don't be greedy and careless. It could lead you to danger.

She saw a big shadow moving in the garden. It was furry and had a long tail. It made a loud roar. Sara was very afraid. She dropped her comb and ran back to her bed. She hid under the covers and cried.

The shadow was a lion. It had escaped from the zoo. It was hungry and looking for food. It saw the comb on the ground. It picked it up and sniffed it. It did not like the smell. It threw the comb away and walked away.

The next morning, Sara woke up and saw the sun. She felt better. She got out of her bed and looked for her comb. She could not find it. She wondered where it went. She did not know that a lion had taken it. She thought maybe it was a dream. She went to the bathroom and used her mom's comb instead. She still liked to play with her hair.

"Look, a bird!" Tom says. "Can we play with it?"

"No, Tom. The bird is not a toy. It belongs to the man over there." Mia says. She points to a man with a gun. He is watching the bird.

"Why does he have a gun?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe he wants to shoot the bird." Mia says.

"That's mean! We have to help the bird!" Tom says.

They sneak behind the man. Tom grabs the gun. Mia opens the cage. The bird flies out.

"Hey, stop!" The man shouts. He is angry. He runs after them.

"Run, Tom, run!" Mia says.

They run away from the man. They find their mom. They tell her what happened.

"You did a brave thing, kids. But you should never touch a gun. It is very dangerous." Mom says.

She hugs them. She is proud of them. She is also worried.

The bird is free. It is happy. It sings a song. It thanks Tom and Mia.

Lily was a sheep who liked to run and play. She did not like to stay with the other sheep in the field. She wanted to see new things and have fun. One day, she saw a big hole in the fence. She thought, "I can go through there and explore!"

She ran to the hole and squeezed through. She felt happy and free. She saw a road, a stream, a hill, and a forest. She ran to each one and looked around. She did not see the farmer who was looking for her.

The farmer was sleepy and worried. He had to find Lily before it got dark. He knew the road, the stream, the hill, and the forest had many dangers for a sheep. He called, "Lily, Lily, where are you?" But he did not hear her answer.

Lily heard the farmer's voice, but she did not want to go back. She thought, "I can hide in the forest and he will not find me." She ran to the forest and hid behind a tree. She did not see the big wolf who was watching her.

The wolf was hungry and sneaky. He saw Lily and licked his lips. He thought, "She is a tasty snack for me." He crept closer and closer to her. He was ready to pounce.

Lily heard a growl behind her. She turned and saw the wolf. She was scared and sorry. She wished she had stayed with the other sheep. She cried, "Help, help, the wolf is here!"

The farmer heard Lily's cry. He ran to the forest and saw the wolf. He grabbed a stick and shouted, "Stop, stop, leave her alone!" He hit the wolf with the stick and chased him away.

Lily ran to the farmer and hugged him. She said, "Thank you, thank you, you saved me!" The farmer said, "You're welcome, you're welcome, but don't run away again!" He took her back to the field and the other sheep.

Lily learned her lesson. She did not run away anymore. She stayed with the farmer and the other sheep. She was happy and safe.

Tom looks for a good place to hide. He sees the fridge. He opens the door and climbs inside. He thinks Lily will never find him there. He closes the door and waits.

Lily counts to ten and starts to look for Tom. She looks under the table, behind the chairs, in the cabinets, but she cannot find him. She wonders where he is. She says, "Tom, where are you? I give up. You win."

Tom hears Lily's voice, but he cannot answer. He tries to open the door, but it is stuck. He feels cold and scared. He wants to get out. He starts to cry.

Lily hears Tom's cry. She follows the sound. She reaches the fridge. She sees the door is closed. She pulls the handle. She opens the door. She sees Tom inside. He is shivering and crying. She says, "Tom, what are you doing in the fridge? You could have frozen. That was a bad place to hide. Come out, quick."

Tom comes out of the fridge. He hugs Lily. He says, "I'm sorry, Lily. I wanted to hide well, but I got trapped. I was very uncomfortable. I thought I would lose you. Please don't be mad at me."

Lily hugs Tom back. She says, "I'm not mad at you, Tom. I'm glad I found you. You are my brother and I love you. But don't ever hide in the fridge again. It is dangerous and not fun. Let's go to the living room and play with our toys. OK?"

Tom nods. He says, "OK, Lily. Thank you for finding me. You are my sister and I love you too. Let's go and play." They hold hands and walk to the living room. They are happy and safe.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. But then they saw some mist in the air. It was white and soft and made everything look fuzzy.

"What is that?" Anna asked.

"It is mist," Ben said. "It is like water, but very small. It comes from the sky when it is cold."

"Can we touch it?" Anna wondered.

"Let's try," Ben said. They ran towards the mist and waved their hands in it. It felt wet and cool on their skin.

"It is fun," Anna said. "But I am getting cold. And I cannot see very well."

"Me too," Ben said. "Maybe we should go back to the slide. It is sunny there."

He looked around, but he could not find the slide. The mist was too thick. He could only see Anna and some trees.

"Where is the slide?" he asked.

"I don't know," Anna said. "I cannot see it either."

They felt scared. They did not like being lost in the mist.

"Maybe we should shout for help," Anna suggested.

"OK," Ben agreed. They shouted as loud as they could.

"Help! Help! We are lost in the mist!"

They hoped someone would hear them and come to find them.

Soon, they heard a voice.

"Anna? Ben? Where are you?"

It was their mom. She had come to the park to pick them up.

"Mom! Mom! We are here!" they shouted back.

They saw their mom walking towards them. She looked worried, but happy to see them.

She hugged them tight and kissed them.

"Are you OK?" she asked.

"Yes, we are OK," they said.

"What were you doing in the mist?" she asked.

"We were playing," they said. "But we got lost. We could not see the slide."

"I'm sorry, sweeties," she said. "The mist can be tricky. It can hide things. You have to be careful."

She took their hands and led them out of the mist. They saw the slide again. It was bright and shiny.

"Can we play on the slide again?" they asked.

"Sure," she said. "But only for a little while. Then we have to go home. It is getting late."

They nodded and smiled. They were happy to play on the slide again. They were happy to have their mom with them. They were happy to be out of the mist.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a tiny hole in the wall of a big house. One day, Timmy saw a big raft floating down the river. He admired the raft and wanted to go on an adventure.

Hootie replied, "No, Timmy. The river can be dangerous. It's better to stay safe in your little hole."

The moral of the story is to always listen to your wise friends and not take unnecessary risks.

When the day of the parade arrived, everybody gathered in the village center. But it was proving to be difficult - the animals kept wanting to do different things. The deer wanted to dance, the birds wanted to sing, and the rabbits wanted to hop! None of them could decide who should go first. 

Then, the chief stepped in. She said, "Let's all go together. We'll dance, sing and hop all at the same time." Everyone agreed and, feeling excited, the animals took to the village center and started their parade, all united as one.

As he was walking, he noticed a small door in one of the buildings. He walked up to it and tried to open it. But the door was closed tight. Toby knocked on the door and it opened.

He walked inside and it was very dark. He heard noise from a room ahead, so he went to investigate.

When Toby walked in, he saw a cat. 

"Hello there," said Toby.

"Meow," said the cat.

Toby said goodbye to the cat and made his way out of the city. He knew he would never be able to find his way back to the little door, but he would never forget all the toys he found there. 

The end.

The moral of the story is: You should eat your meal and take care of your toys. You can love them, but you have to treat them right.

The voice said, "No, we can't be friends. You are a fox and I am a bunny. We are different and we don't get along. Now go away or I will call my dog."

Sam felt hurt and angry. He did not like to be rejected and yelled at. He thought that Ben was rude and silly. He said, "Fine, I don't want to be your friend either. You are a bunny and I am a fox. We are different and we don't get along. I will go away and I don't care about your dog."

"Or maybe it is for Mommy and Daddy," Ben said. "Maybe it is their anniversary cake."

They did not know what to do. They both wanted a piece of cake, but they did not want to be naughty.

They decided to ask Mommy. They ran to the living room, where Mommy was reading a book.

"Mommy, Mommy, can we have some cake?" they asked.

Mommy looked at them and smiled. She knew they had seen the cake. She had made it for them, as a surprise.

"Of course, you can have some cake," she said. "But first, you have to do something for me."

"What is it, Mommy?" they asked.

"You have to share the cake with each other," she said. "And you have to be patient and wait until I light the candles and sing a song."

Lily and Ben nodded. They knew how to share and be patient. They loved each other and Mommy very much.

They hugged Mommy and said, "Thank you, Mommy. You are the best."

Mommy hugged them back and said, "You are welcome, my sweeties. You are the best, too."

"Give me your doll!" Ben said.

"No, it's mine!" Anna said.

Ben tried to grab the doll from Anna, but she held it tight. Ben got angry and pinched Anna's arm. Anna cried out loud.

"Ow! That hurts! Mommy!" Anna shouted.

Mommy heard Anna and came to the living room. She saw Ben pinching Anna and Anna crying.

"Ben, what are you doing? Stop pinching your sister!" Mommy said.

Ben let go of Anna and looked down. He knew he was in trouble.

"I'm sorry, Mommy. I wanted her doll," Ben said.

Mommy picked up Anna and hugged her. She checked her arm and saw a red mark.

"Anna, are you okay? Does it still hurt?" Mommy asked.

Anna nodded and sniffed. She was frightened by Ben's pinch.

"A little bit. Ben was mean to me," Anna said.

Mommy kissed Anna's arm and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. Ben shouldn't have pinched you. He needs to learn to share and be gentle."

Mommy looked at Ben and said, "Ben, you need to say sorry to Anna and give her a hug. Pinching is not nice. It hurts and scares people. How would you feel if someone pinched you?"

Ben felt sorry for Anna and for what he did. He went to Anna and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I won't pinch you again. Can I have a hug?"

Anna looked at Ben and saw that he was sorry. She gave him a hug and said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. You can play with my doll if you ask nicely."

Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good sister. Can I play with your doll, please?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be careful with her. She is my favorite doll."

Mommy smiled and said, "That's very kind of you, Anna. And good job, Ben, for saying sorry and asking nicely. You are both good children. Now, why don't you play together nicely and share your toys?"

"Sam, I'm scared," Mia said. "Where are mom and dad?"

"I don't know, Mia," Sam said. "But we have to stay together and look for them."

They held hands and walked along the sidewalk, hoping to find a friendly face. But everyone seemed to be in a hurry, and no one noticed them. They felt very small and alone.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and saw smoke and fire coming from a nearby store. People screamed and ran away from the flames. Sam and Mia were terrified and didn't know what to do.

"Help! Help!" they cried. "We're lost and there's fire!"

A kind man in a blue uniform heard them and came to their rescue. He was a firefighter, and he had a big hose and a helmet. He sprayed water on the fire and put it out. Then he picked up Sam and Mia and carried them to a safe place.

"Don't worry, kids, you're safe now," he said. "I'm going to find your mom and dad. What are their names?"

"Mom is Lisa and dad is Tom," Sam said.

"OK, Sam and Mia, I'll be right back," he said. He used his radio to call for help and gave their names and description.

Soon, Sam and Mia saw their mom and dad running towards them. They hugged them tightly and cried with joy.

"Mom! Dad! We're so sorry, we wandered away and got lost and there was fire and we were scared and..." they said.

"Shh, shh, it's OK, we're here now, we love you, we're so glad you're safe," mom and dad said. They thanked the firefighter for saving their children and apologized for losing sight of them.

The firefighter smiled and said, "You're welcome, I'm happy to help. But next time, don't wander too far, OK? Stay close to your mom and dad, they know the best way to keep you safe in this big, modern city."

The wise owl looked at the rod and said, "Lily, this is a magic rod. You must be careful with it. To get your toy back, you must wave the rod again and say, 'I wish my toy would come back.'"

Lily did as the owl said. She waved the rod and said, "I wish my toy would come back." Just like that, her toy appeared! Lily was very happy and thanked the wise owl. She learned to be careful with the magic rod and never made anything vanish again.

They put away some of their toys, but they left their favorite ones on the floor. They brushed their teeth, but they did not put away their toothbrushes. They climbed into their beds, but they did not close their eyes.

They waited until Mom left the room. Then they whispered to each other.

"Let's play with the cars," Ben said.

"No, let's play with the dolls," Lily said.

They got out of their beds and reached for their toys. But they both wanted the same toy. They grabbed it and pulled it.

"Give it to me!" Ben said.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said.

They started to fight over the toy. They yelled and pushed and kicked. They made a lot of noise.

Mom heard the noise. She came back to the bedroom. She saw Lily and Ben fighting over the toy. She was not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mom said. "You are supposed to be sleeping. You are making a mess of your bedroom. And you are hurting each other."

She took the toy away from them. She put it on the shelf. She made them put away the rest of their toys and their toothbrushes. She tucked them into their beds. She turned off the light.

"Now, no more fighting," Mom said. "You need to sleep. You have a big day tomorrow. You are going to the zoo with Grandma and Grandpa. You don't want to be sleepy and grumpy, do you?"

Lily and Ben shook their heads. They said they were sorry. They said they loved each other. They said they loved Mom.

Mom kissed them good night. She said she loved them too. She said she was proud of them. She said they were good twins.

Lily and Ben closed their eyes. They felt sleepy. They stopped fighting. They dreamed of the zoo.

"I tried to help the yeast," Sara said. "I made the dough tight so it would increase."

Mom shook her head. "Sara, that is not how it works. You cannot make the dough increase by squeezing it. You have to let it rest and give it space. The yeast needs air and warmth to do its job. If you make the dough tight, you will ruin it. Now we have to start over."

"Wow, Tom! You are smart! The ball looks better now. Thank you for repairing it!" Lily said.

They played together all day long. But when the sun went down, the big, green frog became very hungry. He looked at Ben and thought he would make a tasty snack. So, the frog ate Ben, the polite beetle, with his sharp little horn.

And that was the end of Ben, the polite beetle.

Sue said, "I will help you, but you must finish your lunch first." Tim was not happy, but he knew he had to finish his lunch to get help.

After Tim finished eating, Sue came to help him. They both tried to open the box together. It was still very hard. They pushed and pulled, but the box did not open. Tim and Sue started to fight. They both wanted to open the box first. "I want to open it!" said Tim. "No, I want to open it!" said Sue.

Soon, they both felt sorry for fighting. They said sorry to each other and decided to work together. With one big push, the box finally opened. Inside, they found a lot of toys to play with. Tim and Sue were very happy. They learned that working together was better than fighting.

His mom said, "That is a razor. It is for grown-ups to use, not for kids. It can hurt you, so please put it back."

Tim wanted to be a good boy, so he put the razor back where he found it. He asked his mom, "Can I help you with something else?" His mom thought for a moment, and then she suggested, "Why don't you help me make a sandwich for lunch?"

Together, they made a regular sandwich with bread, cheese, and ham. Tim felt happy that he could help his mom, and they enjoyed their lunch together. From that day on, Tim knew that the razor was not for him to play with, and he always tried to help his mom with other things.

Finally, Lily realized that it's okay to ask for help sometimes. She asked Timmy to help her stand on the chair, and she got the toast. From that day on, Lily learned that it's important to ask for help when you need it.

"Who is there?" Ben asked.

"I am a mole," a voice said. "Please stop poking me."

Ben was curious. He wanted to see the mole. He said, "Can you come out? I want to be your friend."

The mole was scared. He did not like the sun or the noise. He said, "No, thank you. I like to stay in my hole. It is dark and quiet."

Ben did not give up. He said, "Please, just for a little while. I will show you some fun things. I will lead you to the pond, where you can see the fish and the frogs. I will lead you to the tree, where you can see the birds and the squirrels. I will lead you to the field, where you can see the flowers and the butterflies."

The mole was tempted. He had never seen those things before. He said, "Well, maybe for a little while. But you have to be careful. I am not used to the wild. There are many dangers out there."

Ben promised to be careful. He helped the mole out of the hole. He held his hand and led him to the pond. The mole saw the fish and the frogs. He was amazed. He said, "Wow, they are so shiny and hoppy."

Ben smiled. He said, "Yes, they are. Do you want to see more?"

The mole nodded. He said, "Yes, please."

Ben led him to the tree. The mole saw the birds and the squirrels. He was astonished. He said, "Wow, they are so colorful and furry."

Ben laughed. He said, "Yes, they are. Do you want to see more?"

The mole nodded. He said, "Yes, please."

Ben led him to the field. The mole saw the flowers and the butterflies. He was dazzled. He said, "Wow, they are so pretty and flappy."

Ben clapped. He said, "Yes, they are. Do you like the wild?"

The mole smiled. He said, "Yes, I do. Thank you for showing me."

Ben hugged him. He said, "You are welcome. I am glad you are my friend."

But then, they heard a loud roar. A big cat was coming. It had sharp teeth and claws. It wanted to eat the mole.

Ben saw a hole in the ground. He said, "Quick, go in there. It is your hole. You will be safe."

The mole did not hesitate. He dived into the hole. He said, "Thank you, Ben. You saved me."

Ben said, "You are welcome, mole. I am sorry for the cat. It is very mean."

The mole said, "It is okay. It is the wild. There are good things and bad things. But you are the best thing. You are my friend."

Ben said, "You are my friend, too. I will come back and visit you. But now, I have to go home. My mom is calling me."

The mole said, "Goodbye, Ben. Take care."

Ben said, "Goodbye, mole. See you soon."

Tom tried to help Lily. He threw a stick at the duck to make it go away. But the duck did not like that. It got angry and chased Tom. Tom ran away from the pond, but he forgot his boat. The duck saw Tom's boat and thought, "Maybe this one is tasty."

The duck grabbed Tom's boat in its beak and sailed away with it. Lily saw what happened and felt sorry for Tom. She said, "Don't worry, Tom, I'll share my boat with you. We can still have fun together."

Tom smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "Thank you, Lily, you are very kind. Maybe the duck will bring back my boat someday. Or maybe we can make a new one. But for now, let's sail your boat and have a jolly morning."

Tom was a little boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a new toy car that he got for his birthday. He loved to zoom it around the floor and make noises.

One day, he was playing with his car in the kitchen, when he saw a big cupboard. He wondered what was inside. He pushed a chair to the cupboard and climbed on it. He opened the door and saw many things. He saw boxes and cans and jars and bags. He saw some cookies and some crackers and some candy. He wanted to try them.

He reached for a cookie and took a bite. It was sweet and crunchy. He liked it. He reached for a cracker and took a bite. It was salty and crispy. He liked it too. He reached for a candy and took a bite. It was sour and chewy. He made a face. He did not like it.

"Tom, what are you doing?" He heard his mom's voice. He turned around and saw her. She looked angry. She saw the mess he made. She saw the cookie crumbs and the cracker bits and the candy wrapper. She saw his car on the floor.

"Mom, I was hungry," Tom said. He tried to smile.

"Tom, you know you are not supposed to eat from the cupboard. You have to ask me first. And you have to clean up your toys. You are a big boy now. You have to be careful and responsible," Mom said. She took him down from the chair and gave him a hug. She was not so angry anymore. She loved him.

"Sorry, Mom. I will ask you next time. And I will clean up my toys. Can I have some water, please?" Tom said. He was thirsty.

"Of course, Tom. Here is a glass of water. Drink it slowly. And then we can play with your new car together. How does that sound?" Mom said. She gave him a glass of water and a kiss.

"Good, Mom. I love you. And I love my new car. Can I show you how fast it goes?" Tom said. He drank his water and picked up his car.

"I love you too, Tom. And I love your new car. Yes, you can show me how fast it goes. But not in the kitchen. Let's go to the living room. There is more space there. And no more biting from the cupboard, okay?" Mom said. She took his hand and led him to the living room.

"Okay, Mom. No more biting from the cupboard. Only from my plate. And only when you say so. Come on, let's go. Vroom, vroom!" Tom said. He followed her and made noises with his car. He was happy.

"Let's go find something else, Lily," he said. "Maybe we can find some cookies or candy."

But they did not know that their mom was awake. She heard them. She saw them. She was angry. She came out of the house. She called them.

"Lily! Tom! What are you doing? Come back inside right now! You are in big trouble!"

Lily and Tom heard their mom. They stopped playing. They looked at her. They felt sorry. They ran to her. They hugged her.

"We are sorry, mom," they said. "We just wanted to see the star. It was shining so bright. We made a wish."

"What did you wish for?" their mom asked.

"We wished we could play outside all night," they said.

Their mom shook her head. She said, "That was a silly wish. You need to sleep. Sleep is good for you. It makes you grow and learn. The star will be there tomorrow. And so will I. I love you."

She took them inside. She tucked them in bed. She kissed them good night. She said, "Sleep well, my little stars. You are my wish come true."

Lily and Tom smiled. They felt sleepy. They closed their eyes. They dreamed of the star. It was still shining.

Lila and Ben were having a picnic with their mom and dad. They had sandwiches, apples, and cookies. They also had a big jar of jelly that mom made from the berries they picked in the garden.

"Can I have some jelly, please?" Lila asked.

"Sure, honey. Here you go." Mom said, and gave her a spoon and the jar.

Lila opened the jar and tried to scoop some jelly. But the jelly was very thick and sticky. It did not come out easily. Lila twisted the spoon, but the jelly only stretched and snapped.

"Uh-oh. This jelly is too hard. I can't get it out." Lila said.

"Let me help you." Ben said. He took the jar and the spoon from Lila. He twisted the spoon harder, but the jelly still did not come out. He twisted and twisted, until the spoon broke in half.

"Oops. I broke the spoon." Ben said.

"Oh, no. Now we have no spoon and no jelly." Lila said.

Mom and dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. They saw the broken spoon and the jar of jelly.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

"We tried to get some jelly, but it was too thick and sticky. And then Ben broke the spoon." Lila explained.

"I'm sorry, mom. I twisted too hard." Ben said.

"It's okay, sweetie. It was an accident. Don't worry about the spoon. We have another one." Mom said.

She took the jar and the other spoon. She twisted the spoon gently and slowly. She made a small hole in the jelly. Then she twisted the spoon again and again, until the hole became bigger and bigger. She scooped some jelly and put it on a piece of bread.

"Look, I made a jelly sandwich. Who wants one?" Mom asked.

"Me! Me!" Lila and Ben said.

Mom made two more jelly sandwiches and gave them to Lila and Ben. They took a bite and smiled.

"Mmm, this jelly is yummy. Thank you, mom." Lila said.

"Yes, thank you, mom. And sorry for breaking the spoon." Ben said.

"You're welcome, my loves. And don't worry about the spoon. It's just a thing. You are more important." Mom said.

They hugged and kissed mom and dad. Then they finished their picnic and packed their things. They went home happy and full.

"Yes, I did. I can talk because you gave me a magic glove. It is not a normal glove. It is a glove that makes snowmen talk. Do you want to hear a secret?"

Mia and Leo nodded. They were curious.

"I can also count. Do you want to count with me?"

Mia and Leo nodded again. They liked to count.

Mia and Leo looked at the glove. It had five fingers.

"Five!" they said together.

"One!" they said together.

"Very good. You are right. I have one glove. But I don't mind. I don't need two gloves. I have you. You are my friends. And friends are better than gloves."

Mia and Leo smiled. They hugged the snowman. They were happy. They had a talking snowman. And he had a magic glove. It was a very unusual day.

One day, Sara and Ben go to the hospital with their mom and dad. The doctor says he has a new lung for Sara. He says he will take Sara to a room and give her the new lung. Ben is happy for Sara. He hopes she will feel better.

But then, another doctor comes. He says he has a boy who also needs a new lung. He says the boy is very sick and will die soon. He says he wants to give the new lung to the boy instead of Sara. He says it is fair.

Sara's mom and dad are angry. They say it is not fair. They say Sara needs the new lung too. They say they love Sara and want her to live. They argue with the other doctor.

Sara and Ben hear the argument. Sara is scared. She does not want to die. She does not want the boy to die either. She loves her brother and her parents. She says to Ben, "I want to share. Maybe we can give half of the new lung to the boy and half to me. Then we can both breathe well."

Ben hugs Sara. He says, "You are very kind, Sara. But I don't think it works that way. I think you need a whole lung to breathe well. I wish I could give you my lung. But then I would die. And I don't want to die either."

Sara and Ben cry. They do not know what to do. They do not know who will get the new lung. They do not know who will live and who will die.

The story ends with a bad ending. The moral value of the story is that sometimes life is not fair and there are no easy solutions. The story also shows that Sara is generous and brave, and that Ben loves his sister.

You can tell other people to respect and care for the valley. You can be the valley's guardians."

I will learn to respect and care for the valley. I will be the valley's friend."

Lila and Ben forgave the truck driver. They invited him to join them in their work. They restored the valley with their love and their actions. They became the valley's friends and guardians. The valley was happy and healthy again.

The moral of the story is: Love and respect nature, and nature will love and respect you. You can make a difference with your words and deeds. You can restore what is broken with your heart and hands.

Lucy understood and, feeling a bit more relaxed, watched out the window one more time until it was time to go to bed. With all the snow and winter fun fading from her memory, Lucy was anxious and sad, but also excited for all the new things to come.

John was very upset. He wanted to make his dream come true. But his kind mother had refused to help him. So John stopped dreaming. He never tried to fly to the stars again.

John wanted to go to the park, but his mother said he had to wait. She said if he didn't delay, she would make him a special treat. 
John was very excited and waited hard in the corner. But the wait seemed long and his legs got very sore. 
Finally, Mom said it was time to go! He ran outside to the park and saw a flame in the snow. 
John was so excited and hopped around the flame. His mom said it was too hot but John thought it was fun to play the game.
John and Mom played together until the sun went down. When it was time to go, John skipped back to town. 
John had enjoyed a fun day, but he remembered what his mother said: the most important thing was to delay ahead.

Her mom smiles and puts down her book. She takes Sara's papers and looks at them. She says, "Wow, Sara, these are very pretty! You are very good at printing!"

Sara beams and hugs her mom. She says, "Thank you, mom! Can I put them on the wall?"

Her mom nods and says, "Of course, you can. Let's find some tape and a good spot for them."

They walk to the kitchen, where there is a roll of tape on the counter. Sara reaches for it, but she is too short. She tries to jump, but she slips and falls. She hits her head on the floor and feels dizzy.

She cries and says, "Ow, ow, ow! Mom, it hurts!"

Her mom rushes to her and picks her up. She says, "Oh, Sara, I'm sorry! Are you okay? Let me see your head."

She kisses Sara's head and checks for a bump. She says, "You have a little bump, but it's not bad. It will go away soon. You don't need to cry."

She hugs Sara and says, "How about we put some ice on it and then we can put your pictures on the wall, okay?"

Sara nods and says, "Okay, mom. I love you."

Her mom says, "I love you too, Sara. You are my brave girl."

Lily and Sam went to the park with Mom. They saw a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They wanted to play on everything. Mom said they could, but first they had to share a cone. A cone was a sweet thing with ice cream on top.

Mom bought a cone with two scoops, one chocolate and one vanilla. She gave it to Lily and Sam and told them to be careful. Lily and Sam each took a lick of the cone. It was cold and yummy. They smiled at each other.

But then, a big dog came running towards them. It barked loud and jumped on them. Lily and Sam got scared and dropped the cone. The dog ate the cone in one bite. Lily and Sam cried.

"Hey, that's not nice!" Mom said to the dog. She picked up Lily and Sam and hugged them. "I'm sorry, sweeties. The dog was naughty. He should not have taken your cone."

"Can we have another cone, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Please, Mom?" Sam said.

Mom looked at the ice cream stand. It was closed. She shook her head. "I'm sorry, honey. There are no more cones. But we can go home and make some cookies. How does that sound?"

Lily and Sam nodded. They liked cookies too. They wiped their tears and held Mom's hand. They walked home, talking about what kind of cookies they wanted to make. They forgot about the dog and the cone. They were happy.

Lily was a little bird who liked to sing and fly. She had a nest in a big tree with her mom and dad. They were happy and cozy in their nest.

One day, Lily saw a big, hairy animal on the ground. It had four legs and a long tail. It looked at the tree and licked its mouth. Lily was scared. She knew it was a cat, and cats liked to eat birds.

Lily flew to her mom and dad and told them about the cat. They told her to stay in the nest and be quiet. They flew away to find some food. Lily did as they said, but she was still scared.

She watched the cat from the nest. The cat climbed the tree slowly and quietly. It came closer and closer to the nest. Lily wanted to scream, but she remembered to be quiet.

When the cat was almost at the nest, Lily saw something. It was a big, brown dog. It had four legs and a wagging tail. It ran to the tree and barked loudly. The cat heard the dog and stopped. It looked down and saw the dog. It was afraid. It jumped from the tree and ran away. The dog chased the cat and made it scatter.

Lily was happy and relieved. She thanked the dog for saving her. The dog wagged its tail and licked her. Lily liked the dog. She flew to the dog and gave it a hug.

Soon, Lily's mom and dad came back. They saw the dog and Lily. They were surprised and glad. They thanked the dog for being a friend. They invited the dog to share their food. The dog agreed and smiled.

They all ate and talked and laughed. They became good friends. Lily, her mom and dad, and the dog were happy and cozy in their nest.

But the turkey saw them and did not like them. The turkey thought they were trying to take its food. The turkey ran after them and tried to peck them. Tom and Anna were scared. They drove their toy cars as fast as they could. They ran back to the house and shut the door.

Tom and Anna were happy. They hugged Mom and Dad and said sorry for making a mess. They helped to tidy up their toy cars and put them away. They learned not to bother the turkey and to be careful when they drive.

Suddenly, the hole becomes bigger and bigger. Out comes a lot of white fluff. The white fluff flies everywhere. Anna and Ben are surprised and scared. They scream and cry. They think they broke the teddy bear.

Mom hears their scream and cry. She runs to their room. She sees the white fluff and the teddy bear. She is not angry. She is calm and kind. She smiles and hugs Anna and Ben.

"Don't worry, my loves. The teddy bear is not broken. It is just old and worn out. It has a secret inside. Do you want to see?" Mom says.

Anna and Ben followed their mom to the kitchen. They sat on their chairs and looked at their bowls. The soup was green and smelled funny. Ben took a sip and made a face. "Yuck! This soup is bitter. I don't like it," he said.

Anna tried the soup too and agreed. "Me neither. It's icky. Can we have something else, mom?" she asked.

Their mom shook her head. "No, you have to eat your soup. It's good for you. It has spinach and cheese and herbs. It will make you strong and healthy," she said.

Anna and Ben did not want to be strong and healthy. They wanted to be happy and full. They pushed their bowls away and crossed their arms. They did not eat their soup or their bread. They only drank some water.

Their mom was not happy. She said, "If you don't eat your soup, you can't have any dessert. And you have to take a nap after lunch. No more playing for you."

Anna and Ben did not like that. They did not want to nap. They wanted to play. They said, "No, mom. No nap. No soup. We want to play. We want dessert."

Their mom did not listen. She took their bowls and said, "Too bad. You have to nap. It's good for you. It will make you rested and calm. Come on, let's go to your room."

Anna and Ben followed their mom to their room. They did not want to go. They cried and whined and kicked. Their mom put them on their beds and gave them each a cushion. She said, "Here, hug your cushion. It will make you cozy and warm. Now close your eyes and sleep. I'll be back soon."

Anna and Ben did not hug their cushion. They did not close their eyes. They did not sleep. They stayed awake and angry. They said, "We hate soup. We hate nap. We hate cushion. We want to play. We want dessert."

But no one heard them. Their mom was in the kitchen. She ate her soup and bread. She liked them. They were not bitter. They were tasty. She also ate some dessert. She liked it too. It was sweet. It was cake. She smiled and said, "Mmm, this is good. Maybe Anna and Ben will like it too. Maybe they will eat it when they wake up from their nap."

Anna nods. She remembers what mom told her about strangers. But she also likes dogs. She wants to see the dog closer. She notices that the man and the dog are walking away from them. She thinks they will not see her if she follows them.

Suddenly, she hears a loud honk and a screech. She looks up and sees the car stopping right in front of her. She is scared. She screams.

Mom runs to her and hugs her. She is angry and worried. "Anna, what are you doing? You could have been hurt by the car. Why did you leave me and Ben? Why did you follow that dog?"

Anna cries. She is sorry. She says, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to see the dog. He was so big and fluffy. I didn't see the car. I didn't hear you."

Mom sighs. She is glad that Anna is safe. She says, "I know you like dogs, Anna. But you have to be careful. You can't go after strangers or their pets. You have to stay with me and Ben. You have to listen to me. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily wanted to make a cake for their mom. They had a book with a cake recipe and some ingredients. But they did not have a cup to measure the flour and the sugar.

"Can we use your cap, Tom?" Lily asked. "It is big and round like a cup."

Tom looked at his cap. He liked his cap. It was blue and had a star on it. He did not want to get it dirty.

"No, Lily. My cap is not for measuring. It is for wearing. And it is my favorite cap," Tom said.

Lily was sad. She wanted to make a cake for their mom. She looked around the kitchen. She saw a bowl, a spoon, a knife, and a lazy cat. The cat was sleeping on the table. It did not care about the cake.

"Can we use the cat, Tom?" Lily asked. "It is soft and fluffy like flour and sugar."

Tom laughed. He thought Lily was funny. He did not think the cat would like to be used for measuring.

"No, Lily. The cat is not for measuring. It is for petting. And it might scratch us if we try to use it," Tom said.

Lily was sad. She wanted to make a cake for their mom. She looked around the kitchen again. She saw a jar, a fork, a plate, and a clock. The clock was ticking on the wall. It told them the time.

"Can we use the clock, Tom?" Lily asked. "It is round and has numbers like a cup."

Tom looked at the clock. He thought Lily was smart. He did not know if the clock would work for measuring.

"Maybe, Lily. But how do we use the clock for measuring?" Tom asked.

Lily thought for a moment. She had an idea.

"We can use the fork to scoop some flour and some sugar. Then we can put them on the plate. Then we can count how many times the clock ticks until the plate is full. That is how we measure," Lily said.

Tom thought Lily's idea was clever. He agreed to try it.

"Okay, Lily. Let's use the clock for measuring. But we have to be quick. Mom will be home soon and we want to surprise her with the cake," Tom said.

Lily and Tom used the fork, the plate, and the clock to measure the flour and the sugar. They followed the recipe and mixed the ingredients. They put the batter in a pan and baked it in the oven. They made a cake for their mom. They were happy and proud. They hoped their mom would like it.

"No, you can't keep it, Ben," Mia says. "It is not a pet. It is a wild bug. It needs to live in the garden with its friends. Maybe it is a famous beetle. Maybe it has a name and a story."

"A famous beetle?" Ben asks. "What do you mean? How can a beetle be famous?"

Mia thinks for a moment. She remembers a book that her mom read to her. It was about a beetle that went on an adventure.

"Well, maybe this beetle is like the one in the book," Mia says. "Maybe it travels around the world and sees many things. Maybe it helps other bugs and animals. Maybe it has a special skill or a secret."

Ben looks at the beetle with curiosity. He wonders what the beetle's skill or secret is. He wants to know more about the beetle's adventure.

"Can you tell me the story of the beetle, Mia?" Ben asks. "Please, please, please."

Mia smiles. She likes to tell stories. She picks up the beetle gently and puts it on her palm. She looks at Ben and says:

"Okay, I will tell you the story. But first, we have to give the beetle a name. What do you think we should call it?"

Tom and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and serve food to their toys. Tom opened the cabinet and took out some plates and cups. Lily found some spoons and forks in the drawer.

"Who wants some soup?" Tom asked, holding a pot with water and salt. He poured some in a cup and gave it to his teddy bear. "Here you go, Mr. Bear. Be careful, it's hot."

"Who wants some cake?" Lily asked, holding a pan with flour and sugar. She cut a slice and put it on a plate. She gave it to her doll. "Here you go, Missy. It's yummy."

They were having fun until Mom came in. She saw the mess they had made and was upset. She saw the water and salt on the floor, the flour and sugar on the table, and the plates and cups everywhere.

"Tom, Lily, what are you doing?" Mom asked, with a loud voice. "You can't play with these things. They are not toys. They are for cooking. You have to clean up this mess right now."

Tom and Lily were scared. They did not mean to make Mom upset. They just wanted to play. They said sorry to Mom and started to put everything back in the cabinet and the drawer. They also wiped the floor and the table with a cloth.

Mom saw that they were sorry and helped them. She hugged them and said, "I know you were playing, but you have to be careful. These things can be dangerous or make you sick. Next time, ask me before you use them. And if you want to play chefs, I can help you make some real soup and cake."

Tom and Lily smiled and said, "OK, Mom. We love you. Can we have some real soup and cake now?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But first, let's serve some to your toys. They must be hungry too."

Tom and Sara nodded. They said, "Yes, we can. We love each other. We love you too."

Mom and dad smiled. They said, "We love you too. Now, let's clean up this mess and then look at Sara's pictures together. Maybe Tom can help Sara carry them to the kitchen."

Tom and Sara agreed. They hugged each other and picked up the pictures and crayons. They carried them to the kitchen and showed them to their mom and dad. Mom and dad praised Sara's pictures and Tom's help. They all felt happy.

"Ow, that hurt!" Tim cried. He felt sad and angry. He wanted to chase the cat and bite her.

But then he saw a bird on a tree. The bird was singing a pretty song. Tim liked the song. He forgot about the cat and looked at the bird.

"Hi, I am Tim. Do you want to play with me?" he asked the bird.

The bird looked at Tim and smiled. She liked dogs. She thought they were friendly and fun. She flew down and landed on Tim's head.

"Hi, I am Lily. I would love to play with you," she said.

Tim and Lily became friends. They played in the park and had a good time. Tim wagged his tail and Lily sang her song.

Tim learned that not all animals are the same. Some are nice and some are mean. He decided to be nice to everyone and make more friends.

The moral of the story is: Be friendly and you will find friends.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big box of candy under a tree. They were very happy and ran to the box.

"Wow, look at all the candy!" Lily said. "Let's eat some!"

"OK, but we have to share," Tom said. "There is enough for everyone."

They opened the box and took some candy. They ate and ate until they felt sick. They left the box open and went to play on the swings.

Soon, a big rat came and smelled the candy. It crawled into the box and started to eat. It ate and ate until it felt sick. It left the box open and ran away.

The next day, Lily and Tom came back to the park. They wanted to eat more candy. They ran to the box and looked inside. They saw that the candy was all brown and fuzzy. It had rot.

"Yuck, what happened to the candy?" Lily said. "It looks bad."

"It must be the rat," Tom said. "It ate some and left the rest to rot."

They felt sad and angry. They had wasted all the candy. They had not shared with anyone. They had been greedy.

They learned a lesson. They learned that candy is not good for them. They learned that they should not take what is not theirs. They learned that they should share what they have.

They said sorry to each other and to the tree. They threw away the rot candy and went to play with their friends. They decided to eat fruits instead. Fruits are sweet and healthy. Fruits are good for them.

One day, a boy and a girl went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like monkeys, elephants, and giraffes. They liked to watch them and learn their names.

When they came to the lion cage, they saw a big lion with a long mane. He was lying on a rock and looked very sleepy. The boy and the girl wanted to see him roar, so they asked their mom.

"Mom, can we make the lion roar?" they asked.

"No, you can't," their mom said. "The lion is not a toy. He is a wild animal. He might get angry or scared if you make noise. You have to be quiet and respectful."

The boy and the girl nodded. They understood that the lion was not like their cat at home. He was a different kind of animal, and they had to be careful.

But then, they heard a loud roar from another cage. They turned around and saw another lion, but this one was different. He had no mane, and he was smaller and thinner. He looked very angry and sad. He was roaring at the people who were staring at him.

"Mom, who is that lion?" the boy asked.

"That is a lioness," their mom said. "She is a female lion. She is not from here. She is from a faraway place, where there are no cages. She was brought here by some unknown people, who wanted to sell her. But the zoo saved her and gave her a home."

"Does she have a name?" the girl asked.

"Yes, she does," their mom said. "Her name is Nala. She is very brave and strong. She is trying to get used to her new home, but she misses her family and friends. That is why she roars sometimes. She is calling for them."

The boy and the girl felt sorry for Nala. They wished they could help her. They decided to be nice to her and not make noise. They waved at her and smiled.

"Hello, Nala," they said. "We are your friends. We hope you are happy here."

Nala looked at them and stopped roaring. She tilted her head and blinked. She seemed curious and surprised. She gave a small purr and licked her paw.

The boy and the girl were happy. They thought Nala liked them. They hoped she would feel better soon. They thanked their mom for taking them to the zoo. They learned a lot about lions and other animals. They had a fun and interesting day.

One day, they decided to play with their rocket in the backyard. They put on their helmets and suits and climbed inside the rocket. They counted down from ten and pushed a button. The rocket made a loud noise and lifted off the ground.

"Wow, this is so fun!" Sam said. "Look, we are in space!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben agreed. "Look, there is a weird green planet over there. Let's go and see it!"

They steered the rocket towards the planet. It looked like a big ball of slime with eyes and mouths. They landed on the surface and got out of the rocket.

"Hello, weird planet!" Sam said. "We come in peace!"

But the planet did not say hello back. Instead, it opened a big mouth and swallowed the rocket with Sam and Ben inside. They screamed and tried to get out, but it was too late. The planet closed its mouth and burped.

The moral of the story is: Do not go to strange places without asking your parents. You might get into trouble or danger. And always relax and be careful when you play with your toys. They are not real and might break or hurt you.

Lily and Tom are playing in the kitchen. They want to make a cake for Mom. They have a big bowl, some flour, some eggs, some milk and some sugar. They also have a spoon, a whisk and a stand.

"Let's mix the flour and the eggs first," says Lily. She cracks an egg and pours it into the bowl. Tom adds some flour and stirs with the spoon.

"Can I use the whisk?" asks Tom. "It makes bubbles."

"OK, but be careful," says Lily. She gives him the whisk and he starts to mix faster and faster. The batter splashes out of the bowl and onto the table, the floor and their clothes.

"Oops!" says Tom. "We made a mess."

Lily laughs. "It's OK, we can clean it later. Let's add the milk and the sugar now."

They pour some milk and some sugar into the bowl and mix again. The batter looks smooth and creamy.

"Can we taste it?" asks Tom.

"Sure, but only a little bit," says Lily. They dip their fingers into the bowl and lick them. The batter is sweet and yummy.

"Yum!" they say together.

"Now we need to bake it," says Lily. "We need the stand."

She gets the stand from the cupboard and puts it on the table. She puts the bowl on the stand and plugs it in. The stand has a button that makes the bowl spin and heat up.

"Mom says this is a magic stand," says Lily. "It can make cakes in minutes."

"Wow!" says Tom. "How do we know when it's done?"

Lily points to a small window on the stand. "We can see the cake through here. When it's big and brown, it's done."

They watch the window and wait. They see the batter rise and change color. They smell the cake and it makes their mouths water.

"Ding!" The stand makes a sound. The cake is done.

Lily and Tom clap their hands. They unplug the stand and take the bowl off. They see a beautiful cake inside. It has a clear top and a soft bottom.

"Let's surprise Mom," says Lily. "She will love it."

They put the cake on a plate and cover it with a cloth. They clean the table, the floor and their clothes. They wash their hands and faces. They look like good children.

They hear Mom coming home. They run to the door and hug her.

"Hi, Mom!" they say. "We have a surprise for you."

They take her to the kitchen and show her the cake.

"Wow!" says Mom. "Did you make this?"

"Yes, we did," says Lily. "We used the stand and we mixed everything."

"It's a magic cake," says Tom. "We hope you like it."

Mom smiles and kisses them. "I'm sure I will. You are so sweet and clever. Thank you, my loves."

They cut the cake and share it. It is delicious. They are happy. They love each other. The end.

Sara was very scared of the doctor. She did not like the big white room with the strange machines and the cold metal bed. She did not like the doctor's coat and the stethoscope around his neck. But most of all, she did not like the needle.

The doctor said he had to give Sara a shot to make her healthy and strong. He said it would only hurt a little bit and then it would be over. He said Sara was a brave girl and he was proud of her. But Sara did not believe him. She did not want the shot. She did not want the needle.

She cried and kicked and hid under the blanket. She said no, no, no. She demanded to go home. She demanded to see her mommy. She demanded to have a candy. She did not listen to the doctor or the nurse. She made a lot of noise and a lot of trouble.

The doctor and the nurse tried to calm Sara down. They tried to talk to her and sing to her and show her pictures of animals. They tried to give her a sticker and a toy and a hug. But Sara did not want any of that. She only wanted the needle to go away.

Finally, the doctor had an idea. He asked Sara if she liked balloons. Sara nodded. She liked balloons. They were colorful and round and floaty. The doctor said he had a special balloon for Sara. He said it was a magic balloon. He said it could make the needle disappear.

He showed Sara a big red balloon. He said he would blow it up and tie it to Sara's arm. He said the balloon would protect Sara from the needle. He said the needle would not hurt Sara at all. He said Sara would not even feel it. He said Sara could keep the balloon after the shot.

Sara was curious. She liked the balloon. She wanted to see the magic. She agreed to try the doctor's plan. She let the doctor blow up the balloon and tie it to her arm. She watched as the doctor took the needle and put it near her arm. She closed her eyes and waited.

She did not feel anything. She did not hear anything. She did not cry or kick or hide. She opened her eyes and saw the needle was gone. She saw the doctor smiling and the nurse clapping. She saw the balloon still on her arm. She felt proud and happy.

The doctor said Sara was very brave and very smart. He said she did a great job. He said she was successful. He said she could go home now. He said she could have a candy. He gave Sara a high five and a sticker and a toy. He said he hoped to see her again soon.

"Inch is so cute," Lily said. "I hope he is happy."

"Me too," Tom said. "But how do we know if he is warm enough?"

They thought for a while. Then they had an idea. They got a blanket and wrapped it around the box. They thought the blanket would keep Inch warm and cozy.

But they did not know that worms do not like to be too warm. They like to be cool and moist. Inch felt hot and dry inside the box. He tried to find a way out, but he could not.

After a while, Tom and Lily went to check on Inch. They unwrapped the blanket and opened the lid. They gasped. Inch was not moving. He was stiff and brown.

They felt very sad and sorry. They buried Inch in the garden and said goodbye. They learned a lesson. They learned that if they want to keep a pet, they have to learn how to take care of it. They have to respect its needs and feelings. They have to be responsible and loving.

She climbed on the boat and looked around. She saw a wheel, a bell, and a flag. She wanted to touch them, but then she heard a voice. It was a man who worked on the boat. He was angry and shouted at Lily. He said she was not allowed on the boat, and she had to get off.

Lily was scared and sad. She ran back to Max, who was waiting for her. She cried and said she was sorry. She said she did not know she was not allowed on the boat, and she did not mean to make the man angry.

Max hugged Lily and said it was okay. He said he was sorry too, for being scared. He said they could play somewhere else, where there were no angry people. He said he liked Lily, and she was his friend.

Lily smiled and said she liked Max too, and he was her friend. She said she was embarrassed, but she was fine. They held hands and walked away from the harbor, looking for a new place to play.

Lily was a gifted girl who liked to draw and sing. She had many colors and papers to make beautiful pictures. She also had a nice voice that made people happy. She wanted to share her talents with others and make them smile.

One day, she decided to make a card for her neighbor, Mr. Lee. He was an old man who lived alone and did not have many friends. Lily thought he might be lonely and sad. She drew a big sun and a flower on the card and wrote "Hello, Mr. Lee. I hope you have a good day. From, Lily." She put the card in an envelope and walked to his door.

She knocked on the door and waited. She heard some footsteps and then the door opened. It was Mr. Lee. He looked surprised and curious. He saw Lily holding the envelope and asked, "What is this, little girl?"

Lily smiled and said, "This is for you, Mr. Lee. It is a card I made. I want to be your friend and make you happy."

Mr. Lee took the envelope and opened it. He saw the card and read the words. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He looked at Lily and said, "Thank you, little girl. This is very kind of you. You are a gifted girl who can draw and sing. I appreciate your card and your friendship."

Lily was glad that Mr. Lee liked her card. She said, "You are welcome, Mr. Lee. Can I sing a song for you?"

Mr. Lee nodded and said, "Yes, please. I would love to hear your song."

Lily sang a song about the sun and the flower and how they provide light and beauty to the world. Mr. Lee listened and clapped his hands. He said, "That was a wonderful song, little girl. You have a lovely voice. You have made my day brighter and happier."

Lily and Mr. Lee became good friends. They often visited each other and exchanged cards and songs. They provided joy and comfort to each other. They were both gifted and grateful.
