"Who do you think this is for?" Lily asked Tom.

"Maybe it is for us!" Tom said. "Maybe someone sent us a present!"

They ran to the package and tried to open it. But it was very hard. They pulled and pushed, but nothing happened.

They looked around and saw a man sitting on a bench. He was reading a book. He looked kind and smart.

"Excuse me, sir," Tom said. "Can you help us open this package?"

The man looked up and smiled. He walked over to the package and examined it.

"This is not a package," he said. "This is a sculpture. It is a work of art. Someone made it to admire, not to open."

Lily and Tom were confused. They did not know what a sculpture was. They did not know what art was.

"What do you mean?" Lily asked. "What is a sculpture? What is art?"

The man explained that a sculpture was something that someone made with their hands, using different materials, like metal, wood, or clay. He said that art was something that someone made to express their feelings, ideas, or stories. He said that art could be beautiful, funny, sad, or anything else.

Lily and Tom listened carefully. They tried to understand. They looked at the package again. They saw that it had different shapes and colors. They saw that it was shiny and smooth. They saw that it was very big and heavy.

They realized that the package was not a package. It was a sculpture. It was art.

They felt a new feeling. They felt curious and amazed. They felt like they wanted to know more.

They decided to admire the sculpture. They walked around it and touched it. They asked the man more questions. They learned new words.

They thanked the man for his help. They said goodbye to the sculpture. They went back to the slide.

They had a lot of fun. They also learned something new. They felt happy and proud.

One day, they go to the park and see a big sign. The sign says: "Seesaw broken. Do not use." Anna and Ben are sad. They want to play on the seesaw.

They see a man with a toolbox. He is wearing a red hat and a red shirt. He is working on the seesaw. He is trying to replace the spring that makes the seesaw move.

"Hello, mister," Anna says. "Can we help you?"

"Hello, little ones," the man says. "I'm sorry, but you can't play on the seesaw right now. The spring is broken. I need to replace it with a new one."

"Can we see the spring?" Ben asks.

"Sure, here it is," the man says. He shows them the spring. It is rusty and bent. "This spring is old and weak. It can't make the seesaw go up and down anymore."

"Wow, that's a bad spring," Anna says.

"Yes, it is. But I have a new spring. Look, it's shiny and strong. It can make the seesaw go up and down very well." The man shows them the new spring. It is silver and coiled.

"Wow, that's a good spring," Ben says.

"Yes, it is. Now, I need to put it in the seesaw. Can you wait for a few minutes?" The man asks.

"Okay, we can wait," Anna and Ben say. They sit on a bench and watch the man work.

Soon, the man is done. He replaces the old spring with the new one. He tests the seesaw. It goes up and down, up and down.

"Yay, the seesaw is fixed!" The man says. He takes off the sign. "Now, you can play on it. Have fun!"

"Thank you, mister!" Anna and Ben say. They run to the seesaw. They take turns to go up and down, up and down. They are happy. They love the new spring.

The dragon was angry. It roared and breathed fire. It tried to bite Sam and Tom. They were scared. They dropped their rods and paddled away. The dragon chased them. It was fast and strong.

They reached the shore and ran to their home. They told their parents what happened. Their parents did not believe them. They said, "Stop lying, boys. There is no such thing as a dragon. You just made up a story."

But Sam and Tom knew the truth. They had seen the dragon. They never went fishing again. They learned their lesson. They should have listened to Tom. He was right. The fish was not fair. It was a trap.

When the cartoon is over, the TV plays music. Sara and Ben want to dance. But they want to dance in different ways. Sara wants to dance like the cat, and Ben wants to dance like the mouse.

"I want to dance like the cat!" Sara says. "The cat is fast and smart!"

"I want to dance like the mouse!" Ben says. "The mouse is cute and clever!"

They start to dance, but they bump into each other. They get angry and push each other. They stop dancing and start crying.

Mom hears them and comes to the living room. She sees them crying and asks what is wrong.

"Sara and Ben want to dance, but they can't agree on how to dance," Mom says. "They are fighting over the cartoon."

Mom hugs them and wipes their tears. She tells them that they can dance in different ways, and still have fun. She tells them that they can take turns to dance like the cat and the mouse, or they can mix and match their moves. She tells them that they are both fast and smart, and cute and clever.

Sara and Ben listen to Mom and say sorry to each other. They hug and smile. They decide to dance together, and try different moves. They have fun and laugh. They thank Mom for helping them.

Mom smiles and joins them. They all dance to the music, and watch the cartoon. They think the music and the cartoon are funny and sweet.

Tim and Sam were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Tim saw a big spike sticking out of the ground. It was shiny and sharp. He wanted to touch it. He left his car and walked towards the spike.

"Tim, no!" Sam shouted. "That is bad! That can hurt you!"

Tim did not listen. He reached out his hand to grab the spike. But he was clumsy. He tripped over a rock and fell on the spike. He felt a big pain in his arm. He cried out loud.

Sam ran to him and saw the blood. He was scared. He paused and did not know what to do. He wanted to help Tim, but he did not know how.

He saw their mom coming out of the house. She heard Tim's cry and saw the spike. She was angry and worried. She picked up Tim and took him inside. She told Sam to follow her.

She cleaned Tim's wound and put a bandage on it. She hugged him and told him he was brave. She also told him he was silly. He should not touch things that can hurt him. He should listen to Sam.

Tim said he was sorry. He said he was curious. He said he loved Sam. Sam said he loved Tim too. He said he was sorry he could not stop him. He said he was glad he was okay.

Mom smiled and kissed them both. She said they were good brothers. She said they could play with their cars again, but only in a safe place. She said they should be careful and happy. They said they would. They hugged mom and each other. They learned a lesson.

Lily and Ben are going to camp with Mom and Dad. They are very happy. They pack their bags with clothes, toys and snacks. They get in the car and drive to the woods.

When they get to the woods, they find a good spot to stay. Dad sets up the tent and Mom makes a fire. Lily and Ben help by collecting sticks and stones. They see many animals and plants. They say hello to a squirrel, a bird and a flower.

At night, they eat yummy food by the fire. Mom makes soup and bread. Dad makes hot dogs and marshmallows. Lily and Ben love the hot dogs and marshmallows. They are sweet and sticky. They drink milk and water.

After they eat, they sing songs and tell stories. Mom tells a story about a princess and a dragon. Dad tells a story about a pirate and a treasure. Lily and Ben listen and laugh. They are not scared of the dark. They have a flashlight and a lantern.

When they are tired, they go to the tent and sleep. They snuggle in their sleeping bags and hug their teddy bears. They dream of the woods and the animals. They are happy and warm. They like to camp.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a doll and Tom had a figure. The figure was a superhero who could fly and fight bad guys. Tom liked to make the figure zoom around and make noises.

"Look, Sara, my figure can fly!" Tom said, holding the figure in the air.

"That's nice, Tom, but can you be quiet?" Sara said, brushing the doll's hair. "Mommy is working and she said we have to behave."

Tom did not listen. He made the figure fly faster and louder. He pretended the figure was fighting a smelly monster who wanted to eat the doll. He threw the figure at the doll and knocked it off the couch.

"Hey, stop that!" Sara cried, picking up the doll. "You are being mean and rude. You are not behaving at all."

Tom laughed. He thought it was funny to make Sara angry. He grabbed the figure and ran to the kitchen. He wanted to find something else to play with.

Sara followed him. She was very mad. She saw Tom open the fridge and take out a cheese. The cheese was old and smelly. Tom thought it was perfect for the figure. He put the cheese on the figure's head and said, "Look, Sara, my figure has a hat!"

Sara wrinkled her nose. She hated the smell of the cheese. She said, "That's gross, Tom. That's not a hat, that's food. You are wasting food and making a mess. You are not behaving at all."

Tom laughed again. He did not care. He threw the figure with the cheese at Sara. The cheese hit Sara's face and stuck to her hair. Sara screamed. She was very upset. She said, "That's it, Tom. I'm telling Mommy. You are in big trouble."

Tom stopped laughing. He realized he had gone too far. He said, "No, Sara, don't tell Mommy. I'm sorry. I was just playing. Please don't be mad."

But Sara did not listen. She ran to Mommy and told her everything. Mommy was not happy. She scolded Tom and made him clean up the mess. She also took away his figure and said he could not play with it for a week. Tom felt bad. He wished he had behaved better. He said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I'm sorry, Sara. I won't do it again."

Sara forgave him. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I still love you. But next time, please be nice and quiet. And don't play with smelly cheese."

Tom nodded. He said, "I will, Sara. I will." He hugged her and said, "You are the best sister ever."

Sara smiled. She said, "You are the best brother ever. Sometimes." They laughed and hugged again. Mommy smiled too. She said, "That's better. Now, who wants a snack?"

Sara and Ben were playing on the shore. They liked to make sand castles and dig holes. They also liked to watch the waves and the birds.

"Look, Ben, a funny bird!" Sara said, pointing to a big white bird with a long neck and a big beak. "What is it?"

Ben looked at the bird and said, "I think it is a swan. It can swim and fly. It is very pretty."

The swan was swimming near the shore, looking for fish. It saw Sara and Ben and came closer. It was curious about the children and their sand castles.

"Hello, swan!" Sara said, waving her hand. "Do you want to play with us?"

The swan nodded its head and made a soft sound. It liked to play with the children. It let them touch its feathers and feed it some bread. It also helped them make a bigger sand castle with its beak.

Sara and Ben were very happy. They had a new friend. They played with the swan for a long time.

But then, the sun started to go down. It was time to go home.

"Bye, swan!" Sara said, giving it a hug. "Thank you for playing with us. We hope to see you again."

"Bye, children!" the swan said, giving them a smile. "You are very kind and fun. I hope to see you again, too."

Sara and Ben waved goodbye to the swan and ran to their parents. They told them about their new friend and their sand castle.

The swan watched them go. It was sad to leave them, but it was also happy to have met them. It flapped its wings and flew away.

Sara and Ben looked back at the shore. They could not see the swan anymore. It had vanished in the sky. They wondered where it had gone.

They hoped to see it again someday.

Lily was a brave girl who loved to swim. She liked to splash in the water and make bubbles with her mouth. She had a blue swimsuit with a fish on it. She always wore it when she went to the pool with her mom.

One day, Lily was swimming in the pool when she felt a pain in her arm. She had bumped into the wall and hurt herself. She cried and got out of the water. Her mom hugged her and said they had to go to the doctor.

At the doctor's office, Lily was scared. She saw a big machine that looked like a box. The doctor said it was an x-ray. He said it could take a picture of her bones and see if they were broken. He asked Lily to lie down on a table and put her arm inside the box. He said it would not hurt, but it would make a funny noise.

Lily was brave and did what the doctor said. She heard the x-ray make a beep and saw a flash of light. Then the doctor showed her the picture of her arm. He said she had a small crack in her bone, but it would heal soon. He gave her a bandage and a sticker. He said she could swim again in a few weeks.

Lily was happy and thanked the doctor. She hugged her mom and said she was sorry for crying. Her mom said she was proud of her for being brave. She said they could go home and watch a movie. Lily smiled and said she wanted to watch Finding Nemo. She loved fish and swimming. She hoped her arm would get better soon.

Timmy liked to hop. He hopped all the time. He hopped in the park, he hopped in the house, he hopped in the bed. He hopped so much that his mom and dad called him Hoppy Timmy.

One day, Timmy went to a party. There were balloons, cake, and a clown. Timmy liked balloons and cake, but he did not like the clown. The clown had a big red nose, a funny hat, and big shoes. The clown made jokes and tricks, but Timmy did not laugh. He thought the clown was stupid.

The clown saw that Timmy did not like him. He wanted to make Timmy laugh. He walked up to Timmy and said, "Hello, little boy. Do you want to see a magic trick?" Timmy shook his head. He did not want to see a magic trick. He wanted to hop.

The clown did not listen. He took out a big rubber ball and said, "Watch this. I can make this ball disappear." He threw the ball in the air and caught it with his big shoe. He said, "Ta-da! The ball is gone!" He smiled and waited for Timmy to clap.

But Timmy did not clap. He did not think the trick was magic. He saw the ball in the clown's shoe. He thought the clown was stupid. He said, "That's not magic. That's silly. The ball is in your shoe. I can see it."

The clown was surprised. He looked at his shoe and saw the ball. He felt embarrassed. He said, "Oops. You're right. The ball is in my shoe. How did you know?" He tried to laugh it off, but he felt silly.

Timmy did not care. He said, "You're a stupid clown. You can't do magic. You can't make me laugh. You can't hop." He turned around and hopped away. He hopped to the balloons, he hopped to the cake, he hopped to his mom and dad. He was happy. He was Hoppy Timmy.

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play with hoops. They roll them, spin them, and jump through them. They have fun with hoops.

One day, they see a big hoop in the park. It is shiny and colorful. Sam and Ben want to play with it. They run to the hoop and grab it.

"Let me have it!" Sam says.

"No, it's mine!" Ben says.

They pull and tug on the hoop. They are angry and loud. They do not share.

A dog comes to the park. He sees the hoop. He thinks it is a toy. He runs to the hoop and bites it. He makes a hole in the hoop. He rubs his nose on the hoop. He is happy and quiet. He likes the hoop.

Sam and Ben stop fighting. They see the dog and the hoop. They are sad and shocked. They have broken the hoop.

"Look what we did!" Sam says.

"We were stupid!" Ben says.

They feel sorry. They go to the dog and pet him. They say sorry to the hoop. They learn to share. They are friends again. They have fun with the dog.

Sara was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had many toys, but she always wanted more. She saw a big doll in the shop and she asked her mom to buy it for her. Her mom said no, they had enough toys at home. Sara was angry and she cried.

She went to her room and she saw a star in the sky. She thought the star could make her wish come true. She closed her eyes and she said, "Star, star, please give me the big doll. I want it so much." She waited for the star to answer, but nothing happened. She was confused and she cried some more.

The next day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a little boy who had no toys. He was sitting on a bench and he looked sad. Sara felt sorry for him and she remembered how she had many toys at home. She decided to do something nice. She ran to her mom and she asked, "Mom, can I give one of my toys to the boy? He has none and I have many." Her mom smiled and said yes, that was very kind of her.

Sara picked her favorite teddy bear and she gave it to the boy. The boy was surprised and happy. He hugged the teddy bear and he thanked Sara. Sara felt happy too. She realized that she did not need the big doll. She had enough toys and she could share them with others. She looked at the sky and she said, "Star, star, thank you for not giving me the big doll. I made a better wish today."

The moral of the story is: Be grateful for what you have and be generous to others.

One day, Mom says, "Lily and Max, you have to separate. Lily, you go to Grandma's house. Max, you stay with me. We have to do some things."

Lily and Max are sad. They do not want to separate. They want to play together on the lawn.

"Why, Mom?" Lily asks.

"Because Grandma is sick. She needs some help. And I have to go to the store. It is only for a little while. You will see each other soon. I promise." Mom says.

Lily and Max hug each other. They say, "I love you. I will miss you."

Mom takes Lily to the car. Max waves goodbye. He watches them drive away.

Max feels lonely. He does not want to play on the lawn by himself. He sits on the porch and waits for Mom.

After a while, Mom comes back. She has a surprise for Max. She gives him a beautiful flower. It is red and yellow and smells nice.

"Look, Max. This is for you. I saw it at the store and I thought of you. You are my beautiful boy. I love you." Mom says.

Max smiles. He hugs Mom and the flower. He says, "Thank you, Mom. I love you too. Can I put the flower on the lawn?"

"Of course, you can. Let's go together." Mom says.

They go to the lawn. They find a spot for the flower. They dig a hole and plant it. They water it and pat it.

Max feels happy. He has a beautiful flower on the lawn. He thinks of Lily. He hopes she is happy too. He says, "Mom, can we call Lily and tell her about the flower?"

"Sure, we can. Let's go inside and call her." Mom says.

They go inside and call Lily. Lily is happy to hear from them. She tells them about Grandma and her house. She says she misses them.

Max tells her about the flower and the lawn. He says he misses her too.

They say, "I love you. I will see you soon."

They hang up and smile. They know they will play together on the lawn again. They are twins. They are always together in their hearts.

One day, her mom had to go to the store and left Lily with her dad. Lily wanted to surprise her mom with some muffins when she came back. She asked her dad if they could bake some. She thought it needed more water to make it smooth and moist. She told her dad, but he said no, they had to follow the instructions exactly.

They poured the batter into the cups and put them in the oven. Lily set the timer and waited. She hoped the muffins would be good. She wanted to make her mom happy.

Sara's mom saw what was happening and came to stop Sara. She said, "Sara, that is not your car. That is the boy's car. You cannot take things that belong to other people. That is not nice. How would you feel if someone took your cars?"

Sara thought for a moment. She realized that she would feel sad and mad if someone took her cars. She realized that she was being mean to the boy. She felt sorry and let go of the car. She said, "I'm sorry, boy. I was wrong. You can have your car. Can we play together?"

The boy stopped crying and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Sara. I'm sorry, too. We can play together. Do you want to try my car? It is easy to drive."

Sara nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, please. Your car is very cool. Can I show you my cars, too? I have many cars of different colors and sizes."

The boy said, "Yes, please. I would like to see your cars. I like cars a lot."

Sara and the boy became friends and played with their cars happily. Sara learned to share and be kind. She realized that playing with others was more fun than playing alone.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play together. One day, they went with their mom to the big city. They had to ride the subway to get there. The subway was a long train that went under the ground. It was very loud and fast.

"Mom, can we guess where we are going?" Tim asked.

"Sure, you can guess, but I won't tell you until we get there," Mom said.

"I guess we are going to the zoo, to see the animals," Jen said.

"I guess we are going to the park, to play on the swings," Tim said.

They kept guessing until the subway stopped at a station. Mom told them to follow her and get off the train. But Tim and Jen did not listen. They were too busy guessing and talking. They did not see Mom leave the train. The doors closed and the subway started to move again.

"Mom, where are you?" Jen cried.

"Mom, come back!" Tim shouted.

They looked around and saw that they were alone on the train. There were no other people, only empty seats and windows. They felt very frightened. They did not know where they were going or how to get back to Mom.

They hugged each other and hoped that Mom would find them soon. But Mom did not find them. The subway took them far away, to a place they did not know. They never saw Mom again.

Mom smiled and said, "That is a rare plant, Lily. It is called a twisty plant. It can twist its stem and move its flower to follow the sun. Do you want to see?"

"Stop it, Tim!" Jen says. "I don't like it!"

"What is that?" Sara asked, pointing at it.

"That is an oyster," Dad said, coming closer. "It is a kind of animal that lives in the shell. Sometimes, it makes a pearl inside."

"A pearl?" Ben asked, curious.

"Yes, a pearl. It is a round and shiny thing that people like to wear. It is very rare and precious," Dad said.

"Can we open the oyster and see if it has a pearl?" Sara asked, excited.

"Well, we could, but we should not," Dad said. "The oyster is alive, and it needs its shell to protect it. If we open it, we might hurt it or make it die. We should let it be and put it back in the water."

Sara and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for the oyster. They did not want to hurt it or make it die. They wanted it to be happy and make pearls.

"Okay, Dad, we will put it back," Sara said, nodding.

"Good, I am proud of you," Dad said, smiling. "You are very kind and respectful to the oyster."

When she arrived home, Jenny told her mommy what had happened. Her mommy reassured her, explaining that the triangle was a butterfly and it had just been scared off by Jenny's sudden movement.

Jenny was happy to know that the triangle was just an innocent butterfly. She learned a valuable lesson that day - butterflies are beautiful creatures and should be treated with respect!

It was large and shiny! He uncovered it to reveal a bright, colourful treasure chest. He eagerly opened the lid and jumped in excitement when he saw the contents. Inside was a magical toy that he had always wanted!

He was so happy that he decided to cover the chest with dirt again, so that his special surprise would stay hidden. He wanted it to be his very own secret!

From that day onwards, the little boy always made sure to cover his surprises so they would stay hidden!

Once there was a big wild king. He lived in a big castle and had lots of animals. One day, two of the king's animals, a donkey and a fox, started to quarrel. They argued and argued until the king got angry.

The king didn't like quarrels and wanted the animals to get along. He looked down at them and said, "Stop this quarreling, I don't like it!"

The animals heard him, but they still fought and bickered. The king shouted louder this time, "Stop it! Stop quarreling, or else I'll send you away from my castle!"

The animals were afraid and stopped arguing. They looked up at the king with sad eyes, but still listened to him. The king smiled and said, "Good, that's better. Now be good friends and don't quarrel ever again!" 

The donkey and fox nodded and walked away together. From then on, they were the best of friends and never quarrelled again. All because of the wise wild king.

The moon shone in the sky and Jenny felt brave again. She looked out of the window and smiled. She wasn't scared anymore. Jenny went to bed, holding her stone in her pocket. She was happy knowing she could bravely face anything now.

But then, they see a cord. The cord is long and red. It is on the ground. They are curious.

"What is this?" Ben asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a snake!" Lily says.

They are scared. They drop the leaves and back away. They look at the cord.

But then, they hear a laugh. It is a lively laugh. It is from behind a tree. They see a man. The man is holding a remote. The cord is attached to the remote.

"Hello, kids!" the man says. "Don't be afraid. This is not a snake. This is a toy car. The cord is to control the car. See?"

The man pushes a button. The toy car moves. It makes a beep. It has lights.

Lily and Ben are surprised. They are not scared anymore. They are interested.

"Wow! That is a cool toy!" Lily says.

"Can we play with it?" Ben asks.

"Sure!" the man says. "But first, let me help you with the leaves. You worked hard to gather them. Let's make a big hill and jump in it together!"

Lily and Ben are happy. They smile. They say thank you. They help the man with the leaves. Then, they play with the toy car. They have a lively time. They make new friends.

Dad looked up and played along. "Yes, please," he said. "I am a wealthy lady who likes to go on tours. I have a lot of money and a big hat. I like to see the sights and learn new things. Can you take me to the park and the zoo and the museum?"

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Of course. Hop on our bus and we will show you the best places in the city. And if you get hungry or thirsty, we have plenty of supplies for you."

Dad thanked them and got on the bus. He pretended to pay them with paper money and put on his big hat. Anna and Ben drove their bus to the park and the zoo and the museum, which were really the backyard and the bedroom and the bathroom. They told dad about the animals and the plants and the paintings, and gave him some food and water when he asked.

They had a lot of fun playing pretend. They were happy bus drivers who supplied food and water and did tours around the city. They made their mom and dad happy too. They were a happy family.

"Knight Tom, please hurry! The dragon is coming!" Lila says. She holds a stick as a sword and a basket as a shield.

"I am coming, Princess Lila! I have a magic wine to stop the dragon!" Tom says. He runs with a bottle of juice as the wine. He is a reliable knight. He always helps Lila.

They see the dragon. It is a big dog. The dog barks and runs to them. Lila and Tom are not afraid. They are brave.

"Take this, dragon! Drink the magic wine!" Tom says. He splashes some juice on the dog. The dog stops and licks the juice. It likes the juice.

"Good dragon! You are our friend now!" Lila says. She pets the dog. The dog wags its tail. It likes Lila and Tom.

Lila and Tom are happy. They have a new friend. They share the juice and the stick and the basket. They play together until it is time to go home.

"Because we don't own it," Tom says. "We rent it. We had to leave our old house because we had no money. We had a big house with a garden and a dog. But we lost everything. Now we have nothing."

"You have something," she says. "You have me. I live on this street too. I can be your friend. We can play together and share our toys. Maybe you can come to my house and see my cat. Maybe I can come to your house and see your steps. They look fun to sit on."

Lila drew the temple very carefully. She used many colors and shapes. She made the temple look very pretty. Sam drew the temple very quickly. He used only one color and a few shapes. He made the temple look very simple.

"Because I like it more than mine. It is more beautiful." Lila said.

He ran downstairs and saw a big box with a bow. He opened it and saw a stuffed tiger. He was happy but also a little sad. He wanted a real tiger, not a toy. He said to his mom, "Thank you, mom, but this is not a real tiger. Where is my real tiger?"

His mom hugged him and said, "Tommy, I know you love tigers, but a real tiger is not a good present. A real tiger is wild and dangerous. It needs a lot of space and food and care. It does not belong in a house. It belongs in the jungle. A toy tiger is a good friend. You can play with it and cuddle with it and take it anywhere. It will always love you and never hurt you."

Tommy thought about what his mom said. He looked at his stuffed tiger and felt its soft fur and its big eyes. He realized that his mom was right. A toy tiger was a better present than a real tiger. He hugged his mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. You are right. I love my toy tiger. It is the best present ever. Thank you, mom."

His mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tommy. I'm glad you like it. Happy birthday, my sweet boy."

Tommy learned that sometimes what we wish for is not what we need. He learned to be grateful for what he has and to respect the animals and their habitats. He and his toy tiger became best friends and had many adventures together.

"Who is there?" Tom asks.

"Help me, please. I am in the chamber. I have been here for a long time. I am hungry and thirsty. Please, give me some food and water. Please, let me out." A voice says.

"Maybe we should help him. He sounds sad." Sue says.

"Maybe he is bad. Maybe he will hurt us. Maybe we should go." Tom says.

They argue for a while. Then they hear a loud noise. It is the owner of the big house. He is angry. He sees Tom and Sue in the room. He sees the open door. He sees the chamber.

She took the celery and put it on one side of the scale. Then she looked for something else to put on the other side. She saw a big book, a soft teddy bear, and a shiny ball. She tried each one, but none of them matched the celery. The celery was always heavier.

Lily was puzzled. She thought celery was not heavy at all. It was green and thin and crunchy. How could it weigh more than a book or a bear or a ball? She decided to ask her mom.

She brought the celery and the scale to her mom, who was reading on the couch. She showed her mom what she was doing and asked her why the celery was so heavy.

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She explained that celery was mostly water, and water was heavier than air. She said that the book, the bear, and the ball had a lot of air inside them, so they weighed less than the celery. She said that celery was good for you, because it had vitamins and fiber. She asked Lily if she wanted to try some.

Lily nodded. She was curious about the celery. She took a bite and felt the water squirt in her mouth. She liked the taste and the crunch. She decided that celery was not only heavy, but also yummy and mysterious. She thanked her mom and went back to play with her scale. She wondered what else she could weigh.

Lily was a little girl who loved to feed the squirrels in the park. She always brought some peanuts for them and watched them eat and play. One day, she saw a new squirrel who looked very shy and scared. He had a big scar on his tail and he stayed away from the other squirrels.

Lily wanted to be his friend, so she threw a peanut near him and smiled. The squirrel sniffed the peanut and looked at Lily. He was hungry, but he was also afraid. He had been hurt by a mean dog before, and he did not trust people or animals.

"Hello, little squirrel," Lily said softly. "Don't be scared. I won't hurt you. I have more peanuts for you. Come closer, please."

The squirrel hesitated, but he decided to give Lily a chance. He took a step towards her and reached for the peanut. Lily threw another one and another one, until the squirrel was close enough to touch. He felt Lily's hand on his head and he flinched. But Lily was gentle and kind. She stroked his fur and whispered, "You are a brave squirrel. You are a good squirrel. I like you."

The squirrel felt something he had not felt in a long time. He felt warm and safe and happy. He nibbled on the peanuts and cuddled with Lily. He forgot about his scar and his fear. He had found a friend.

Lily and the squirrel became best friends. They met every day in the park and shared peanuts and hugs. Lily taught the squirrel how to play and trust. The squirrel taught Lily how to be patient and compassionate. They learned from each other and they helped each other. They released their worries and their pain. They found joy and love.

The moral of the story is: Be kind to those who are different or hurt. You might make a new friend and heal a broken heart.

She opened the first door and saw some books. She opened the second door and saw some dishes. She opened the third door and saw some toys. She was very happy. She took out some toys and played with them on the floor.

But she did not know that the cabinet was not very strong. It was old and wobbly, and had a crack on the back. When Lily opened the fourth door, the cabinet tilted and fell over. It made a loud noise and broke some dishes. Lily was scared and cried.

Her mom heard the noise and ran to the living room. She saw the mess and Lily. She was angry and worried. She hugged Lily and checked if she was hurt. She was not hurt, but she was very sorry. She said sorry to her mom and helped her clean up. She learned to be more careful when she examined things.

Sara was very happy. Her grandma was coming to visit. Grandma always brought Sara a big chocolate bar. Sara loved chocolate. She wanted to eat it all.

But Sara had a little brother, Ben. Ben also liked chocolate. He wanted to share Sara's chocolate bar. Sara did not want to share. She said, "No, Ben. This is my chocolate. Go away."

Ben was sad. He cried. He said, "That's not fair, Sara. You are spoiled. You have to share."

Mom heard Ben crying. She came to see what was wrong. She saw Sara holding the chocolate bar. She saw Ben with tears in his eyes. She said, "Sara, what are you doing? Why are you making Ben cry?"

Sara said, "Mom, this is my chocolate. Grandma gave it to me. I don't have to share."

Mom said, "Sara, that's not nice. You have to be kind to your brother. Sharing is caring. If you don't share, your chocolate will melt."

Sara looked at her chocolate bar. It was warm and soft. It was starting to melt. She did not want to lose her chocolate. She said, "OK, Mom. I will share. But only a little bit."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Sara. Here, I will cut the chocolate bar in half. You can have one half, and Ben can have the other half."

Sara gave Ben half of her chocolate bar. Ben stopped crying. He said, "Thank you, Sara. You are nice."

Sara said, "You're welcome, Ben. You are nice, too."

They ate their chocolate together. They were happy. Grandma came to visit. She hugged them both. She said, "I'm proud of you, Sara and Ben. You are good children."

But then they heard a loud noise. It came from the house. They ran to see what it was. They saw their mom in the kitchen. She was holding an iron. The iron was hot and steamy. It had burned a hole in a shirt. Their mom looked pale and scared.

"Mom, what happened?" Anna asked.

"I was ironing your dad's shirt, but I forgot to shut the iron off. It got too hot and burned the shirt. Now your dad will be angry with me. He needs the shirt for work tomorrow." Their mom said.

Anna and Ben felt sorry for their mom. They wanted to help her. They had an idea.

"Mom, don't be sad. We have a gift for you. Come with us." Ben said.

They took their mom to the garden. They showed her their bucket. It was full of bugs. There were worms, beetles, spiders, and snails. They had collected them all.

"Look, mom. We found these for you. They are your new friends. You can play with them and forget about the shirt." Anna said.

Their mom smiled. She hugged them and thanked them. She was not pale anymore. She was happy.

"Thank you, Anna and Ben. You are very sweet and thoughtful. I love you and your gift. But maybe we should let the bugs go back to their homes. They might not like the bucket very much." She said.

They agreed. They let the bugs go. They watched them crawl and fly away. They felt good. They had made their mom happy. They went back to the house. They shut the iron off. They ate some cookies. They had a good day.

"Look, Ben, a bunny!" Sara said. "Let's go get it!"

They ran towards the bushes, holding their nets. The furry animal heard them and turned around. It was not a bunny. It was a skunk.

The skunk was scared and angry. It lifted its tail and sprayed a stinky liquid at Sara and Ben. They got hit in the face and clothes. They screamed and dropped their nets.

"Yuck, yuck, yuck!" Sara cried. "It's not a bunny, it's a skunk!"

"Run, run, run!" Ben shouted. "It smells so bad!"

They ran away from the skunk, but it was too late. They were covered in the stinky liquid. They smelled so bad that no one wanted to play with them. Not even their club friends.

They had to go home and take a bath. They had to throw away their nets and clothes. They had to say sorry to their mom and dad. They had to stay inside for a long time.

They learned a hard lesson. They should not chase furry animals in the bushes. They should not judge by looks. They should be careful and respectful of nature.

They were very sad. They wished they had never seen the skunk. They wished they had stayed with their club. They wished they had a real bunny.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. They also liked to look at the flowers. There were many colors and shapes of flowers, but their favorite was the sunflower. The sunflower was big and yellow and had a happy face.

One day, they saw a bee flying near the sunflower. The bee was black and yellow and had a loud buzz. Tom and Lily were curious and wanted to see the bee closer. They ran towards the sunflower and the bee.

"Hello, bee!" Tom said. "Can we play with you?"

The bee did not like to be disturbed. He was busy collecting nectar from the sunflower. He did not want to play with Tom and Lily. He felt angry and scared. He zoomed away from the sunflower and towards Tom and Lily.

"Go away, children!" the bee said. "This is my sunflower! You are too noisy and too close! You might hurt me or the sunflower!"

Tom and Lily did not understand the bee. They thought he was rude and mean. They did not want to go away. They wanted to catch the bee and touch the sunflower. They kept running after the bee and the sunflower.

The bee felt more angry and scared. He zoomed faster and faster. He tried to sting Tom and Lily to make them go away. Tom and Lily felt pain and fear. They cried and ran away from the bee and the sunflower.

They ran back to their house. They told their mom what happened. Their mom hugged them and put some ice on their stings. She also explained to them why the bee was angry and scared.

"The bee was not rude and mean, Tom and Lily," she said. "He was just doing his job. He was collecting nectar from the sunflower to make honey. He also helped the sunflower to grow more seeds. He was afraid that you would hurt him or the sunflower. He only stung you to protect himself and the sunflower."

Tom and Lily felt sorry for the bee and the sunflower. They realized that they were wrong to chase them and to touch them. They learned to respect the bee and the sunflower and to keep a safe distance from them.

"Hello, children!" the bee said. "Thank you for your apology. I am sorry for stinging you. I was just afraid and angry. I think you are brave and kind. You can watch me and the sunflower, but please do not touch us. We are delicate and need space."

Tom and Lily nodded and smiled. They watched the bee and the sunflower from a safe distance. They learned to appreciate the bee and the sunflower and to share the garden with them. They also learned to zoom with their eyes, not with their hands.

Lily thought about what her mommy said and decided to be kind to the boy. The next day, she saw him again and asked if he wanted to play with her yarn. The boy was surprised but accepted her offer. They had a lot of fun together and became friends. From then on, Lily knew that it was always better to be kind than to be rude.

When Timmy got to the store, he saw a big toy truck that he really wanted. But the toy truck cost more money than Timmy had. Timmy felt sad that he couldn't buy the toy truck. Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high up in the sky and feel the wind in her feathers. One day, Tweety saw a big green tree in the distance and decided to fly towards it. 

As Tweety got closer to the tree, she noticed something strange. There was a confused squirrel running around the trunk of the tree. Tweety didn't know what was wrong, but she knew she wanted to help. 

Tweety landed on a branch near the squirrel and chirped, "What's wrong?" The squirrel explained that he had lost his favorite acorn and couldn't find it anywhere. Tweety knew just what to do. She soared up into the sky and searched for the acorn from above. 

After a few minutes, Tweety spotted the acorn on the ground below the tree. She flew down and picked it up with her beak, then brought it back to the squirrel. The squirrel was overjoyed and thanked Tweety for her help. From then on, they were the best of friends and would often play together under the big green tree.

He quickly grabbed the filthy bread and threw it at the wolf. The wolf was so surprised that he stopped chasing Ducky and started eating the bread instead. Ducky was safe and happy, and he learned that sometimes even filthy things can be useful.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a cozy hole in a big house. One day, Timmy smelled some yummy cheese coming from the kitchen. He followed the smell and saw a big grill with cheese on it.

Timmy wanted to eat the cheese, but he was too small to reach it. He tried to climb up the grill, but he fell down. Then, Timmy met a wise old cat named Whiskers. "Hello, little mouse. What are you doing?" Whiskers asked.

"I want to eat the cheese on the grill, but I can't reach it," Timmy said.

Whiskers said, "You can escape from the grill by being modest. Ask the humans for help, and they will give you the cheese."

Timmy was shy, but he listened to Whiskers. He asked the humans for help, and they gave him the cheese. From that day on, Timmy learned that being modest and asking for help is a good thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a clever rabbit who lived in a forest. One day, he went to a nearby pond to drink some water. But when he got there, he saw a big lion sitting next to the pond.

The lion said, "Hey rabbit, I am thirsty. Can you order some water for me?"

The rabbit thought for a moment and said, "Sure, I will bring you some water. But first, let me tell you something. You are very strong and powerful, but you don't need to order me around. It's always better to ask nicely."

The lion realized his mistake and said, "I'm sorry rabbit. Can you please bring me some water?"

The rabbit happily went to the pond and brought back some water for the lion. From that day on, the lion and rabbit became friends and always asked nicely when they needed something. The moral of the story is that it's important to treat others with kindness and respect.

Tom tried to read the sign, but he did not know all the words. He only knew "tap" and "use".

"It says... tap... use..." Tom said, sounding unsure.

"So we can use it?" Anna asked.

Tom nodded. He did not want to admit he did not know the rest. He was ignorant of the sign's meaning.

He turned the tap harder, hoping water would come out. But instead, he heard a loud hiss and a spray of water. The water was hot and it burned his hand. He screamed and dropped the pot. The water splashed everywhere, on the floor, on the walls, on them.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried, shaking his hand.

"Tom, what did you do?" Anna asked, scared and wet.

They heard footsteps and saw their mom running into the kitchen. She saw the mess and the sign and the tap.

"Tom, Anna, what have you done?" she asked, angry and worried. "Didn't you see the sign? The tap is broken! You can't use it! You have to wait for the plumber to replace it!"

Tom and Anna looked at each other and felt ashamed. They did not see the sign. They did not know what it meant. They were ignorant and careless. They said sorry to their mom and helped her clean up the water. They learned their lesson and never played with the tap again.

Tom and his mom were worried. They tried to open the door, but it was locked. Tom had an idea. He saw a big flower pot on the porch. He pushed it to the window and climbed on it. He looked inside and saw the elderly lady on the floor. She looked scared and hurt.

"Hello, lady. We are here to help you. We have some food and other things for you. Can you reach the window?" Tom said.

The elderly lady smiled and nodded. She crawled to the window and grabbed Tom's hand. Tom helped her get up and sit on the window sill. He gave her a bag of food and a bottle of water. She thanked him and drank some water.

"You are a very brave and kind boy. What is your name?" she asked.

"My name is Tom. This is my mom. She works for the store. We deliver things to people who need them." Tom said.

"Well, Tom, you and your mom are very good people. You saved me. I was alone and afraid. But now I have some food and some friends. Thank you very much." she said.

Tom and his mom smiled. They were happy to help the elderly lady. They called for an ambulance to take her to the hospital. They waited with her until it came. They waved goodbye and promised to visit her again. They went back to their car and continued their work. They felt good about what they had done. They had delivered more than just things. They had delivered hope and kindness.

Anna liked to design things. She used paper, crayons, scissors and glue to make pictures and shapes. She wanted to make a telephone, like the one her mom used to talk to grandma. She cut out a big circle and a small circle from a yellow paper. She glued them together and drew some buttons on the small circle. She cut out a long strip from a green paper and glued it to the big circle. She made a hole in the middle of the strip and put a string through it. She tied a knot at the end of the string and glued a red paper cup to it. She had made a telephone!

She was very proud of her design and showed it to her mom. "Look, mom, I made a telephone! Can I call grandma with it?" she asked.

Mom smiled and hugged her. "That's a very nice telephone, Anna. But it's not a real telephone, it's a pretend one. You can't call grandma with it, but you can play with it and pretend to talk to her."

Anna was a little sad, but she understood. She decided to play with her telephone anyway. She put the big circle to her ear and the red cup to her mouth. She said, "Hello, grandma, this is Anna. How are you?"

She waited for an answer, but there was only silence. She pulled the string and looked at the red cup. It was empty. She wondered where the voice came from.

She heard a knock on the door. It was grandma! She had come to visit. She saw Anna's telephone and smiled. "What a lovely telephone, Anna. Did you make it yourself?" she asked.

Anna nodded and ran to hug her. "Yes, grandma, I made it. But it doesn't work. I tried to call you, but you didn't answer."

Grandma laughed and kissed her. "That's because I was on my way here. I wanted to surprise you. But you know what? I have a real telephone in my bag. Do you want to see it?"

Anna's eyes lit up. She said, "Yes, please, grandma. Can I hold it?"

Grandma took out her telephone from her bag. It was big and heavy and shiny. It had a lot of buttons and a screen. She said, "This is my telephone. I use it to talk to people who are far away. Do you want to try it?"

Anna nodded and reached for the telephone. But it was too heavy for her. She dropped it on the floor. It made a loud noise and cracked. Grandma gasped and Anna cried. Mom came to see what happened. She saw the broken telephone and the sad faces. She said, "Oh, no, grandma, I'm so sorry. Anna didn't mean to break your telephone. She was just curious."

Grandma sighed and hugged Anna. She said, "It's okay, Anna. Don't cry. It was an accident. I know you didn't mean to break it. You were just trying to design a new way to talk to me. Anna smiled and wiped her tears. She said, "Yes, grandma, we can. I love you, grandma."

Grandma said, "I love you, too, Anna. And I love your telephone."

They were about to give up, when they saw a sign on the cooler. It said: "To open the cooler, solve this riddle: What has a face and two hands, but no arms or legs?" They thought hard. They looked around. They saw a clock on the wall. It had a face and two hands, but no arms or legs.

They shouted: "The answer is a clock!" They typed the word "clock" on the lock. It clicked and opened. They were happy. They took some drinks and shared them. They learned that if they use their brains, they can solve problems. They were successful. They thanked the cooler and the riddle. They enjoyed their drinks and their friendship.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big hole in the ground. It has a sign that says "trap". Tom thinks it is a joke. He wants to go near the hole and wave to Sam.

"Look, Sam, I can wave to you from the hole!" Tom says. He runs to the hole and jumps over it. He lands on the other side and waves to Sam.

Sam is scared. He thinks the hole is bad. He does not want to go near the hole. He shouts to Tom. "Tom, come back! The hole is bad! It is a trap!"

But Tom does not listen. He thinks Sam is silly. He wants to show Sam that the hole is not bad. He jumps over the hole again. But this time, he slips and falls into the hole. He screams and cries. He is stuck in the trap.

Sam hears Tom scream and cry. He feels sorry for Tom. He runs to the hole and looks down. He sees Tom in the trap. He is hurt and scared. Sam wants to help Tom. He calls for help. "Help! Help! My friend is in the trap!"

Soon, a man comes to the park. He hears Sam call for help. He sees the hole and the sign. He knows it is a trap. He has a rope and a ladder. He throws the rope to Tom and tells him to hold on. He puts the ladder in the hole and climbs down. He helps Tom out of the trap. He takes him to the doctor.

Tom is safe now. He is sorry for being silly. He thanks the man and Sam for helping him. He learns a lesson. He will not go near bad traps again. He will listen to Sam next time. He will be a good friend.

"Can we have some ice cream, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can choose one flavor each," Mom said.

Lily and Ben ran to the vendor and looked at the pictures of the ice cream. Lily picked chocolate and Ben picked lemon.

The vendor gave them each a cone with a scoop of ice cream. They thanked him and paid him with Mom's money.

Lily licked her chocolate ice cream and smiled. It was sweet and creamy. Ben licked his lemon ice cream and frowned. It was sour and bitter.

"Yuck, I don't like this," Ben said.

"Here, you can have some of mine," Lily said. She offered her cone to Ben.

"Really? Thank you, Lily," Ben said. He took a bite of Lily's chocolate ice cream and liked it much better.

Lily and Ben shared their ice cream and enjoyed it together. Mom watched them and smiled. She was happy that they were kind and generous.

One day, Tom went to visit his grandma. His grandma was old and walked with a cane. She liked to sit on her chair and knit. She did not have any toys for Tom. Tom thought his grandma was boring. He wanted to play with his car, but he left it at home.

"Grandma, can I play with your cane?" Tom asked. He thought the cane looked like a stick that he could use to hit things.

"No, Tom, you cannot play with my cane. It is not a toy. It helps me walk. If you take it, I will fall down," his grandma said. She did not like Tom's idea.

"But I have nothing to play with here. Your house is boring. I want to go home and play with my car," Tom said. He was angry and sad.

"Tom, you should not be rude to your grandma. She loves you and wants to spend time with you. Why don't you sit with me and I will tell you a story? A story about when I was a little girl like you. Maybe you will find it interesting," his grandma said. She smiled and patted the chair next to her.

Tom did not think his grandma's story would be fun, but he had no choice. He sat with her and listened. He was surprised to hear that his grandma had many adventures when she was young. She told him about how she rode a horse, climbed a tree, and flew a kite. She showed him pictures and gave him cookies. Tom started to like his grandma's story. He forgot about his car and his cane. He learned that his grandma was not boring. She was brave and funny and kind. He hugged his grandma and said, "I love you, grandma. Thank you for telling me your story."

They ran to the kitchen and saw their mom holding the broken cake. She looked sad and angry.

"We're sorry, mom, we did it," Lily said, holding her red magnet.

"We didn't mean to, mom, we were just playing," Ben said, holding his blue magnet.

Their mom sighed and put the cake on the table. She looked at Lily and Ben and saw that they were sorry.

"It's okay, kids, I know you didn't do it on purpose. But you have to be careful with magnets. They can be dangerous and cause trouble. You have to be polite and ask before you use them on other things," she said.

He decided to bury his aeroplane in the dirt. He dug a hole with his hands and put the aeroplane inside. He covered it with dirt and patted it down. He said, "Goodbye, aeroplane. You were my favourite toy. I will miss you."

He walked back to the house, feeling very sorry for himself. He did not notice that Spot followed him, wagging his tail. Spot felt sorry for Tommy too. He wanted to make him happy again. He had an idea.

He ran back to the garden and dug up the aeroplane. He carried it in his mouth and brought it to Tommy. He dropped it at his feet and licked his face. He wagged his tail and barked, trying to say, "I'm sorry, Tommy. I didn't mean to hurt your aeroplane. I just wanted to play with you. Can we still be friends?"

Tommy looked at Spot and then at the aeroplane. It was still broken, but it was not buried anymore. It was out in the open, where he could see it. He felt a little bit better. He smiled and hugged Spot. He said, "It's okay, Spot. I forgive you. You are my best friend. Maybe we can find another toy to play with together."

They went inside the house and looked for a new toy. They found an enormous ball that was red and blue. They took it outside and played with it. They had fun. They were happy.

"Or a baby dragon!" Tom said. "Let's take it home and see what hatches."

They picked up the egg and ran to Tom's house. They put the egg in a box and waited for it to crack. They were very excited and curious.

But the egg did not crack. It started to shake and make noises. Then it burst open and a wild animal jumped out. It had fur and claws and teeth and horns. It roared and scratched and bit everything in sight. It was not a bird or a dragon. It was a monster!

"Help!" Lily and Tom screamed. "This is not a fun egg! This is a bad egg!"

They ran out of the house and called for help. A man came and saw the mess. He was angry and scared. He said the egg was from the zoo and it was very rare and dangerous. He said Lily and Tom should not have taken it. He said they were lucky they were not hurt.

Lily and Tom felt sorry and ashamed. They said they were sorry and they learned their lesson. They said they would never take things that did not belong to them. They said they would be more careful and respectful of nature.

The man forgave them and took the egg and the monster back to the zoo. He said he hoped they would come and visit the animals there, but only with permission and supervision. He said they could still play and have fun, but they should also be wise and responsible.

Lily and Tom agreed and thanked the man. They hugged each other and went back to the park. They decided to play with a ball instead of an egg. They had fun and they were happy. They also were more wild.

Finally, they arrived at the park. Lily saw a big slide and wanted to go down it. She stepped up the stairs with her left foot and slid down the slide. It was so much fun! As they left the park, Lily was tired but happy. She hugged her mommy and said, "Today was the best day ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside in the garden. One day, he found an old apple on the ground. The apple was starting to rot and it didn't smell very nice. Tim knew that he shouldn't eat it, so he threw it away.

Later that day, Tim's mom told him about oxygen. She said that we need oxygen to breathe and stay alive. Tim thought that was very interesting. He took a deep breath and felt the air go into his lungs.

Before going to bed, Tim's mom asked him to tidy up his toys. Tim didn't like tidying up, but he knew it was important. He put all of his toys in their proper places and made sure everything was neat and tidy. Then he went to bed, feeling proud of himself for being so responsible.

Once upon a time, there was a small bird named Tweetie. Tweetie loved to play in the trees and hop from branch to branch. One day, Tweetie's favorite branch broke and she fell to the ground. 

"Oh no!" cried Tweetie. "My branch is broken. What will I do?"

"Don't worry," said her friend, a wise old owl. "You can replace your branch with a new one."

"But where will I find a new branch?" asked Tweetie.

"Just look around," said the owl. "There are many small branches on the ground. You can pick one and make it your new home."

So Tweetie looked around and found a small branch that was just right for her. She picked it up with her beak and flew back to her tree. Now she had a new branch to play on and hop from. She was very happy and thanked her wise old friend for his help.

The next day, the lady came back with a big bag. Inside the bag were many seeds. She planted the seeds all around the field. Then, she told the field to wait and be patient.

After some time, the seeds grew into beautiful flowers and tall trees. Animals came to live in the field too. The field was no longer boring. It was now a happy place, full of life and color. And the field and the lady lived happily ever after.

They liked to shoot water at each other, at the plants, and at the birds. But they knew they had to be careful not to shoot water at the things in the house, because their mom and dad would be angry.

One day, they were playing with their water gun in the backyard, when they saw a big, shiny toilet in the corner. It was a new toilet that their dad had bought, but he had not installed it yet. Anna and Ben were curious about the toilet, and they wanted to see how it worked. They ran to the toilet, and Anna lifted the lid. She saw a lot of water inside, and she had an idea.

"Let's shoot water at the toilet!" she said to Ben. "Maybe it will make a funny sound!"

Ben thought it was a good idea, too. He aimed his water gun at the toilet, and pulled the trigger. He shot water at the toilet, and waited for the sound. But nothing happened. He shot water again, and again, and again. Still nothing.

"Maybe it's broken," he said to Anna.

"Maybe we need to shoot more water," she said.

They both shot water at the toilet, until their water gun was empty. They looked at the toilet, and saw that it was full of water. They wondered what would happen if they flushed it.

"Let's flush it!" Anna said.

"OK!" Ben said.

They pushed the handle, and the toilet flushed. But instead of going down, the water came up. It came up very fast, and very high. It splashed all over Anna and Ben, and all over the backyard. It made a loud noise, and a big mess.

Anna and Ben were wet, and shocked, and scared. They heard their mom and dad coming out of the house. They looked at them, and saw that they were angry.

"What did you do?" their mom asked.

"We shot water at the toilet," Anna said.

"Why did you do that?" their dad asked.

"We wanted to hear a funny sound," Ben said.

They realized that they had done something bad. They felt sorry, and ashamed.

"We're sorry, mom and dad," they said.

Their mom and dad sighed, and hugged them.

"We're glad you're OK, but you have to be more careful," their mom said. "You can't shoot water at things that are not meant for water. You could have broken the toilet, or hurt yourself, or someone else."

Their dad said, "You have to respect the things that we have, and use them properly. You can't just play with them, without thinking of the consequences."

Anna and Ben nodded, and said, "We understand, mom and dad. We won't do it again."

Their mom and dad said, "We love you, but you have to learn from your mistakes. Now, let's clean up this mess, and then you can play with your water gun again. But only in the right places, and with the right things."

Anna and Ben said, "OK, mom and dad. Thank you."

They helped their mom and dad clean up the mess, and then they played with their water gun again. But this time, they only shot water at each other, at the plants, and at the birds. And they had fun, without making trouble. They learned their lesson, and they were happy.

Anna liked to write in her diary every day. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams and her feelings. She kept her diary in a secret place under her bed, where no one could find it.

One day, her brother Tom was looking for his ball in her room. He saw a pink book under her bed and pulled it out. He opened it and saw Anna's writing and drawings. He wanted to read it and see what she wrote.

"Hey, what is this?" he asked, holding the diary.

Anna heard him and ran into her room. She saw Tom with her diary and felt angry and scared. She wanted her diary back.

"Tom, give me that! That is my diary! It is not for you!" she shouted, trying to grab the diary.

Tom was bigger and stronger than Anna. He held the diary high and laughed.

"No, I want to read it. Maybe you wrote something funny or silly. Let me borrow it for a while," he said, teasing her.

Anna felt tears in her eyes. She knew Tom would not be nice and would make fun of her. She wished she was brave and could get her diary back.

She thought of her favorite superhero, who always helped people and fought bad guys. She imagined she was like him and had superpowers. She decided to be brave and stand up to Tom.

She jumped on the bed and reached for the diary. She pulled it hard and Tom lost his balance. He fell off the bed and dropped the diary. Anna caught it and hugged it.

"Ha! I got it! You can't borrow it! It is mine!" she said, feeling proud and happy.

Tom rubbed his head and felt sorry. He realized he was mean and hurt Anna's feelings. He got up and apologized.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I was wrong. I should not have taken your diary. It is yours and it is private. You are brave and smart. Can you forgive me?" he said, looking at her with a sad face.

Anna looked at him and saw he was sincere. She remembered he was her brother and she loved him. She smiled and forgave him.

"It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. But don't do it again. And don't tell anyone what you saw in my diary. It is a secret," she said, putting her diary back under her bed.

Tom nodded and hugged her. He said he would not tell anyone and he would be nice to her. They made up and played together. Anna was glad she was brave and got her diary back. She wrote about it in her diary that night.

Lily sees a root that sticks out of the ground. She thinks it is a good step. She puts her foot on the root and pushes. But the root is broken. It snaps and Lily falls down. She hurts her knee and cries.

Ben hears Lily cry and runs to her. He sees her knee is red and has a small cut. He feels sorry for Lily. He decides to help her. He picks a leaf from the tree and puts it on her knee. He says it will make her feel better.

Lily stops crying and smiles at Ben. She says thank you. She thinks Ben is a good friend. She decides to share her toy car with him. They play with the car on the grass. They forget about the tree and the broken root. They are happy.

Ben and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a big pond with many ducks and swans. Ben liked the swans. He wanted to touch them. He ran to the edge of the pond and reached out his hand.

"Ben, stop!" Mom shouted. "The swans may bite you. They are strong and can hurt you."

But Ben did not listen. He wanted to pet the swan. He saw a white swan with a long neck and a red beak. He thought it was pretty. He moved closer to the swan.

The swan did not like Ben. It did not want him to touch it. It hissed and flapped its wings. It snapped its beak at Ben's hand. Ben was scared. He pulled back his hand and cried.

Lily saw what happened. She ran to Ben and hugged him. She said, "It's okay, Ben. The swan was just protecting itself. You should not bother the swans. They are not toys. They are living things. They have feelings too."

Ben nodded. He was sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, swan. I did not mean to make you angry. You are beautiful and strong. I will not touch you again."

Mom came and wiped Ben's tears. She said, "That's good, Ben. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Next time, we can watch the swans from a distance and enjoy their beauty. They are amazing animals, but they need their space."

Ben and Lily agreed. They said, "We love the swans, but we will respect them." They waved goodbye to the swans and went to play on the swings. They had fun at the park.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play at the zoo. They loved to see the animals and make noises like them. One day, they saw a big gorilla who was eating a banana. The gorilla looked very strong and hairy.

"Let's go closer and say hello to the gorilla," Tim said. He was not afraid of anything.

"No, Tim, we have to stay behind the fence. The gorilla might be angry or scared," Sam said. He was more careful and smart.

But Tim did not listen to Sam. He climbed over the fence and ran towards the gorilla. He wanted to touch the gorilla and give him a hug. He did not see the wet peel of the banana that the gorilla had thrown away.

Tim stepped on the wet peel and slipped. He fell down and hurt his knee. He cried out loud. The gorilla heard him and turned around. He saw Tim on the ground and got angry. He thought Tim was trying to take his banana. He roared and showed his big teeth.

Sam was very scared for Tim. He ran to the fence and shouted, "Help, help, the gorilla is mad at Tim!"

A zookeeper heard Sam and came quickly. He used a stick to make the gorilla go away. He picked up Tim and brought him back to the fence. He gave him a band-aid for his knee and a hug for his tears.

"Tim, you were very naughty and foolish. You should never go near the animals without permission. They can be dangerous and hurt you. You are lucky that the gorilla did not bite you. You have to listen to your brother and follow the rules," the zookeeper said.

Tim felt very sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, zookeeper. I'm sorry, Sam. I was wrong. I won't do it again. I love the gorilla, but I will only watch him from far away."

Sam forgave Tim and hugged him. He said, "I'm glad you are okay, Tim. I love you, too. Let's go and see the other animals. But this time, we will stay behind the fence and be safe."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of obedience, safety, and respect for animals.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play in the forest. She had a red bow in her hair and a blue dress. She liked to look for flowers and animals, but she was afraid of talking to other children.

One day, she saw a boy in the forest. He had a green hat and a brown coat. He was holding a bow and arrow. He looked friendly, but Lily was too shy to say hello. She hid behind a tree and watched him.

The boy saw a bird on a branch. He aimed his bow and arrow at the bird. He was about to shoot, when Lily shouted, "No! Don't hurt the bird!"

The boy was surprised and turned around. He saw Lily behind the tree. He lowered his bow and arrow and smiled. He said, "Hi, I'm Tom. Who are you?"

Lily was scared, but she also felt sorry for the bird. She came out from behind the tree and said, "I'm Lily. Please don't hurt the bird. It's very pretty and sings nice songs."

Tom looked at the bird and nodded. He said, "You're right. The bird is very pretty and sings nice songs. I won't hurt it. I was just pretending to be a hunter. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She said, "Yes, I want to play with you. You seem nice. Can I see your bow and arrow?"

Tom handed his bow and arrow to Lily. He said, "Sure, you can see them. They are not real, they are just toys. I made them myself. Do you like them?"

Lily took the bow and arrow and looked at them. She said, "Yes, I like them. They are very cool. You are very clever. Can you teach me how to use them?"

Tom said, "Of course, I can teach you. It's easy and fun. Come, let's find a target."

Lily and Tom ran to a clearing in the forest. They found a big tree with a round mark on it. Tom said, "This is our target. We have to try to hit the mark with our arrows. Do you want to go first?"

Lily said, "Yes, I want to go first. Can you help me?"

Tom said, "Sure, I can help you. Here, hold the bow like this, and the arrow like this. Then pull the string back and aim at the mark. Then let go of the string and watch the arrow fly."

Lily did as Tom said. She held the bow and arrow, pulled the string back, aimed at the mark, and let go of the string. The arrow flew through the air and hit the mark. Lily was very happy. She said, "Wow, I did it! I hit the mark!"

Tom clapped his hands and said, "Well done, Lily! You are very good! You hit the mark on your first try! That's amazing!"

Lily and Tom hugged each other and laughed. They felt very happy and proud. They became friends and played in the forest for a long time. They forgot about their shyness and had fun. They also left the bird alone and listened to its songs. They had a wonderful day in the forest.
