One day, they find a big hill. It is green and soft. They want to go up the hill. They hold hands and climb. They are happy.

When they reach the top, they see a big sky. It is blue and bright. They see clouds and a sun. They feel a wind. It is cool and gentle.

"Look, Ben!" Lily says. "The clouds are moving. They are like shapes. I see a bunny. Do you see it?"

"Yes, Lily!" Ben says. "I see it too. And I see a car. And a star. The clouds are fun."

They lie on the hill and watch the clouds. They make stories with the shapes. They are quiet and calm.

Then, Lily has an idea. She jumps up and says, "Ben, let's spin!"

"What is spin?" Ben asks.

"Spin is when you turn around and around. Like this!" Lily says. She shows him how to spin. She spreads her arms and twirls. She feels dizzy and happy.

"Wow, Lily! That looks fun. I want to spin too!" Ben says. He joins her and spins. They spin and spin and spin. They giggle and shout.

They spin so fast that they fall down. They roll on the hill. They feel the grass and the wind. They see the sky and the clouds. They are dizzy and happy.

They stop and look at each other. They smile. They hug.

They are twins. They like to play outside in nature. They are happy.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. The park has a big hill. Lily and Ben like to run up and down the hill.

One day, Lily and Ben see a big bird in the sky. The bird is black and white. It has a long neck and a big beak. Lily and Ben think the bird is nice.

"Look, Ben, a nice bird!" Lily says.

"Wow, Lily, a nice bird!" Ben says.

They want to say hello to the bird. They wave their hands and call to the bird.

"Hello, nice bird! Come here, nice bird!" they call.

But the bird does not come. The bird flies away. It flies to the west. The west is where the sun goes down.

"Bye, nice bird! Come back soon, nice bird!" they call.

They watch the bird until it is gone. Then they smile at each other and run up and down the hill again. They are happy. They hope to see the nice bird again.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. Today, they have a new quiz. The quiz is about animals. Sara and Ben want to do well.

They go to the park and see a big tree. The tree has many branches. Sara and Ben see something on a branch. It is a picture of an animal. The picture is hanging from a string.

"What animal is this?" Sara asks Ben.

Ben looks at the picture. He sees a long nose, big ears and gray skin. He knows the answer.

"It is an elephant!" Ben says.

"Good job, Ben!" Sara says. "You are smart."

They look for more pictures. They find a picture of a lion, a picture of a fish and a picture of a bird. They know all the answers. They are happy.

They finish the quiz. They see a sign on the tree. The sign says: "Well done, Sara and Ben! You know a lot about animals. Love, Mom and Dad."

Sara and Ben smile. They hug each other. They love their new quiz. They love their mom and dad. They have fun in the park.

Sam and Lily were playing in the park. It was a sunny day and they liked to run and jump on the grass. But the sun was very bright and it hurt their eyes.

"Let's make sunglasses!" Sam said. He had an idea. He ran to a big tree and picked some leaves. He gave some to Lily and said, "Put these on your eyes. They will block the sun."

Lily did what Sam said and put the leaves on her eyes. She smiled and said, "Now we have sunglasses! We look cool!"

They walked around the park with their leaf sunglasses. They saw a dog. The dog was hairy and brown. He wagged his tail and barked.

"Hello, dog!" Sam said. He wanted to pet the dog. He took off his leaf sunglasses and reached out his hand.

But the dog did not like Sam's sunglasses. He thought they were food. He jumped and snatched the leaves from Sam's hand. He ate them and licked his lips.

"Hey, that's not nice!" Sam said. He was sad. He liked his sunglasses.

Lily saw what happened and felt sorry for Sam. She took off her leaf sunglasses and gave them to Sam. She said, "Here, you can have mine. I don't need them. You are my friend."

Sam smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. You are my friend too."

They put on their leaf sunglasses again and continued to play in the park. They did not mind the dog. They were happy.

Lily liked to play sport with her friends. They had a big ball and they kicked it to each other. Sometimes they ran after the ball and sometimes they threw it in the air. Lily was good at sport. She could kick the ball very far and catch it very well.

One day, Lily and her friends played sport in the park. They had a lot of fun. They laughed and shouted and jumped. Lily kicked the ball very high and ran to catch it. But she did not see a big tree in front of her. She bumped into the tree and fell down. She felt dizzy. She saw stars and birds and colors. She closed her eyes and rubbed her head.

Lily's friends came to help her. They asked her if she was okay. They gave her some water and a hug. Lily opened her eyes and smiled. She said she was okay. She was just dizzy. She wondered why she saw stars and birds and colors. She wondered if the tree was magic. She wondered if she could kick the ball again.

Lily's friends told her that she saw stars and birds and colors because she hit her head. They said it was not magic. They said it was normal. They said she should rest for a while. They said they would play sport with her again when she felt better.

Lily nodded and thanked her friends. She lay down on the grass and looked at the sky. She saw clouds and sun and blue. She felt calm and happy. She liked to play sport with her friends. She liked to wonder about things. She liked to be Lily.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with blocks and make symbols. A symbol is a shape that means something. For example, a heart means love and a star means wish.

One day, Lily and Tom are playing with blocks in the park. They make a big heart symbol with red blocks. They are happy and proud of their symbol.

But then, a big boy comes and kicks their symbol. The blocks fall down and break. The big boy laughs and runs away.

Lily and Tom are sad. They hear their symbol crack and crash. They cry and hug each other.

"Why did he do that?" Lily asks.

"I don't know. He is mean and rude." Tom says.

They look at their broken symbol. They feel like their love is broken too.

But then, they see something. A little girl comes and picks up a red block. She smiles and gives it to Lily.

"Hi, I'm Mia. I like your symbol. It's very pretty. Can I help you make it again?" She says.

Lily and Tom are surprised. They wipe their tears and smile too.

"Hi, I'm Lily. This is Tom. Thank you for your help. Yes, you can help us make it again." Lily says.

They take the red blocks and start to make the heart symbol again. Mia helps them and adds some yellow blocks for the sun.

Soon, they finish their symbol. It is bigger and brighter than before. They are happy and proud of their symbol again.

They hear their symbol shine and sing. They laugh and hug each other and Mia.

They learn that love is stronger than hate. And that a new friend can make a sad day happy.

Sara was very dirty after playing in the mud with her dog. She had mud on her face, her hair, her clothes and her shoes. Her mom saw her and said, "Sara, you need to take a shower right now. You are too dirty to go inside the house."

Sara nodded and followed her mom to the bathroom. She took off her clothes and shoes and put them in a basket. Her mom turned on the water and helped her get in the shower. Sara felt the warm water wash away the mud from her skin and hair. She used soap and shampoo to make bubbles and clean herself. She sang a song while she showered.

When she was done, her mom wrapped her in a big towel and dried her with a hairdryer. Sara liked the feeling of the warm air on her head. She put on her pajamas and brushed her teeth. She felt very clean and cozy.

"Mom, can I read a book before bed?" Sara asked.

"Sure, honey. But only one book. You look very sleepy," her mom said.

They went to Sara's bedroom and picked a book from the shelf. Sara snuggled with her mom on the bed and listened to her read the story. She looked at the pictures and smiled. She felt her eyes getting heavy and her head resting on her mom's shoulder.

"Good night, Sara. I love you," her mom said.

"Good night, mom. I love you too," Sara said.

She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of playing in the mud with her dog again.

Anna and Ben like to play with their toys in the living room. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, books and more. But sometimes they make a big mess and Mom is not happy.

"Anna, Ben, it's time to clean up your toys," Mom says. "Please put them in the baskets. You have one basket for each kind of toy."

Anna and Ben nod and start to organize their toys. Anna puts the dolls in one basket and the books in another. Ben puts the cars in one basket and the blocks in another. They work together and soon the living room is tidy.

"Good job, Anna and Ben," Mom says. "You organized your toys very well. Now you can have a snack and read a story with me."

Anna and Ben smile and hug Mom. They are happy and calm. They like to play with their toys, but they also like to keep them in the baskets.

Tom was a big boy who liked to wear a suit. He had a blue suit with a tie and a hat. He felt very smart and proud in his suit. He wanted to show his suit to his friends at the park.

But when he got to the park, he saw a dog. The dog was big and brown and had sharp teeth. The dog ran to Tom and barked. Tom was scared. He tried to run away, but the dog was faster. The dog jumped on Tom and bit his suit. Tom cried. His suit was torn and dirty.

A lady came and took the dog away. She said sorry to Tom and gave him a hug. She said the dog was not mean, just playful. She said she would buy Tom a new suit. Tom stopped crying. He was still sad, but he was also kind.

He went to his friends and told them what happened. His friends said they were sorry, too. They said they liked Tom, not his suit. They said they would play with him anyway. Tom smiled. He was happy. He had good friends. He did not need a high suit to have fun.

Lily was playing with her doll in her room. She liked to make her doll talk and dance and sing. She did not like to share her doll with anyone. She did not know that her brother Max was watching her from the door.

Max wanted to play with the doll too. He thought the doll was pretty and fun. He waited until Lily went to the bathroom. Then he sneaked into her room and took the doll. He ran to his room and hid the doll under his bed.

Lily came back and saw that her doll was gone. She looked everywhere for her doll. She was sad and angry. She asked Max if he saw her doll. Max said no. He lied. He felt guilty.

Lily did not believe Max. She saw his shadow under his bed. She knew he had her doll. She ran to his bed and pulled out the doll. She yelled at Max. She said he was bad and mean. She said he had to say sorry.

Max was scared and sorry. He said sorry to Lily. He said he would not take her doll again. He said he would play with her if she wanted. Lily was still mad, but she forgave Max. She said he could play with her doll sometimes. They hugged and played together. They were happy.

Sara loves to admire her stamps. She has many stamps with different pictures on them. She has stamps with animals, flowers, cars, and stars. She likes to sort them by color and shape. She puts them in a big book with clear pages.

One day, Sara is very hungry. She wants a snack. She goes to the kitchen and looks for something to eat. She sees a bowl of fruit on the table. She sees a banana, an apple, and a pear. She likes all of them, but she likes bananas the most.

She takes the banana and peels it. She is about to take a bite, when she sees something on the peel. It is a stamp! It has a picture of a monkey on it. Sara thinks it is very funny and cute. She wonders how the stamp got on the banana.

She decides to keep the stamp and add it to her collection. She puts the peel in the trash and eats the banana. She is not hungry anymore. She is happy. She goes back to her room and finds a place for the monkey stamp in her book. She admires her stamps and smiles.
